answer: Four objects chain together. `pm-threshold-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location>/<parameter>` sets the actual limit on one instance: `add`/`set` with `low-threshold` and `high-threshold` (uint64/int64/decimal64, or na / not-supported; default na). `direction` is ingress, egress, all or na (default all) and `location` is all, na, near-end or far-end (default all). `pm-threshold-profile-<resource-type>/<direction>/<location>/<period>/<parameter>` holds the per-resource-type values and exposes `default-low-threshold`, `default-high-threshold`, `min-value` and `max-value`, e.g. `set pm-threshold-profile-OTUC14i/ingress/near-end/pm-24h/errored-seconds high-threshold 1200`. `pm-control-entry-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location>` must have `tca-supervision true` for the crossing to be reported, and `data-supervision true` for the data to be collected; `show` on it also lists `supported-parameters` (max 100 elements). `pm-profile-entry-<resource-type>/<direction>/<location>/<period> default-tca-supervision` sets that for newly created resources.

Three objects. `set ntp ntp-enabled true` (default true) and `set ntp ntp-auth-enabled true` (default false); `assignment-method` is manual, dhcp or both (default both). Then `add ntp-key-<key-id> key-type <value> key-value <value> [is-trusted <value>]` where key-id is 1..65534, key-type is sha-1, aes-cmac, sha-256 or md5, key-value is a string of length 8..40, and `is-trusted` defaults to false, e.g. `add ntp-key-2 is-trusted true key-type sha-1 key-value Infinera`. Then `add ntp-server-<ip-address> auth-key-id <key-id>` (IPv4, IPv6 or DNS name; `auth-key-id` default not-applicable; `origin` manual or dhcp, default manual; `admin-state` default unlock). To verify: `show ntp ntp-active-server`, and `show ntp-server-status-<ip-address>` for `auth-status` (ok, yes, bad, none), `reach` (377 means all recent probes answered), `stratum`, `offset`, `delay`, `jitter` and `condition`. `show clock time-source` should read ntp.

They act on different things. `protection-switch` is the operating command for protection group switching: `protection-switch [-f] [operation-type=]<value> [switch-target=]<value> [protection-group=]<value>`, Operational mode. `operation-type` is force, lockout, manual or release; `switch-target` is not needed for the release and lockout operations. Example: `protection-switch protection-group-test operation-type=force switch-target=protection`. The group itself is defined by `protection-group-<name>` (protection-type y-cable or snc-n, working-pu, protection-pu, reliable-cp), whose `pg-request` and `pg-state` reflect the switch. `manual-switchover [-f] [resource=]<AID>` is the controller command: it moves the active controller card, e.g. `manual-switchover card-1-3`, and warns 'Controller will switchover and connection to the management interface will be lost. Do you want to continue? [y/n]'. Use `-f` to skip the confirmation.

`set-time` is only applicable when time-source is manual, that is when NTP is not enabled, so an enabled NTP is what rejects it. Check `show clock time-source`: values are ntp (NE synchronises via NTP) and manual (NE internal clock), default manual. `show clock` also gives `current-time`, `universal-time`, `timezone` (default Universal-Time-Coordinated), `DST-active` and `last-time-jump` (jumps under 10 seconds are ignored). `time` prints the current system time in the configured timezone. If you really want manual time, `set ntp ntp-enabled false` first; otherwise fix the source with `show ntp ntp-active-server` and `show ntp-server-status-<ip-address>` (`reach` 377 means all recent probes answered, plus `stratum`, `offset`, `auth-status`, `condition`). `set-time` format is ISO 8601 combined date and time, `set-time 2021-02-06T11:16:58Z` for UTC or `set-time 2021-04-01T18:46:44+03:00` for an offset.

Identity: `show ne` gives `ne-id`, `ne-name` (default '1830 GX'), `ne-type` (G30 or G40), `node-type` (ILA, OADM, XPDR), `ne-site`, `ne-location`, `clli`, `node-controller-chassis-name` (default 1), `equipment-discovery-ready`, `alarm-report-ready` and `recover-mode`. Contents: `show equipment`, `show slot` (supported-type, installed-type, current-equipment), `show inventory`, `show card-<name>`, and the `status` / `status equipment` dashboards. Cost: `restart [-h] [-f] [<resource-id>] [<type>] [<sub-component>]`, Operational mode, requires confirmation unless `-f`. With no resource-id it restarts the active controller card. `type` defaults to warm. cold reboots all components and sub-components and is service affecting, connectivity returns within five minutes (cold on XMM4 is not service affecting but visibility is lost); warm reboots only the processor and is non service affecting (XMM4 loses visibility for 3 minutes); shutdown gracefully shuts the card down. Sub-components are listed by `show card resources`.

The chassis holds `slot` and `inventory`, so slot 2 is `slot-1-2` (`show slot-<chassis-name>-<slot-name>` gives AID, supported-type, installed-type, oper-state, avail-state, current-equipment) and the card provisioned there is `card-<name>` created with `add card-<name> required-type <value> chassis-name <value> slot-name 2`. Beneath a `card` hang `comm-eth`, `inventory`, `port`, `property`, `sub-component`, `tom` and `usb`. Beneath a `port` hang `current-fw`, `serdes` and `supported-tom-power`. The pluggable itself is `tom-<card-name>-<port-name>` (`add tom-1-4-T1 required-type QSFPDD`), and its FRU data is read with `show inventory-<card-name>-<port-name>`, e.g. `show inventory-1-3-1`, giving hardware-version, actual-type, actual-subtype, serial-number, clei, vendor, part-number, manufacture-date, insertion-date, number-of-lanes, vendor-compliance-code, actual-power-class (uint8, range 1..8), actual-max-power-draw and fw-status.

Capability of the model is `supported-card`: `show supported-card-<card-type>` returns `supported-subtype`, `default-card-mode`, `supported-card-mode`, `card-width` (na, single-slot, double-slot, half-slot, triple-slot), `card-height` in RUs, `category` (controller, line-card, fan, power-supply, other, carrier-card, blank), `is-field-replaceable`, `max-power-draw` in Watts, `node-type-compatibility` (all, ILA, OADM), `grid-mode-support` (default general-c-band), `supported-bands` (default standardC-band), `console-port-support`, `support-serdes-config` and `location-led-support`. Its ports, slots and pluggables are `supported-port-<card-type>/<port-name>`, `supported-slot` and `supported-tom`. The card actually fitted is `card-<name>`: `show card-1-7` gives required-type, required-subtype, card-mode, power-profile, category, chassis-name, slot-name, max-power-draw, last-reboot-reason, admin-state, oper-state and avail-state. `show capabilities-<name>` retrieves a specific card's capabilities.

The stack must be built bottom-up. `ospf-instance-<instance-id>` (id 0..255) needs `router-id`; `router-id-mode` is manual or use-loopback, default use-loopback, and the stated pre-condition is that with use-loopback an ipv4 LO-MGMT address must be configured. `version` is ospfv2 (default) or ospfv3. `ospf-area-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id>` has the pre-condition that the OSPF instance must be created before the area can be added; `ospf-area-type` is normal. `ospf-interface-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id>/<ospf-if-name>` has the pre-condition that the instance and the area must be present; `enable` defaults true, `hello-interval` default 10, `router-dead-interval` default 40, `ospf-cost` default 10, `priority` default 1. Then `show ospf-neighbor-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id>/<ospf-if-name>/<router-id>` shows how far it got: state down, init, 2-way, exstart, exchange, loading, full, plus role drother/dr/bdr/ptp. Its pre-condition is that the neighbour NEs also have instance, area and interface configured and are connected with DCN interface bridges; an OSPF neighbor is deleted when the OSPF interface goes down.

`show software-load-<location-id>/<swload-state>` is the per-card view, where location-id is <chassis-id>-<slot-id> and swload-state is active, inactive or installable, e.g. `show software-load-1-5/active`. It returns swload-version, swload-manifest, swload-prepared, swload-status, swload-activation-type (direct, warmstart, coldstart), swload-vendor, swload-product, swload-label and swload-pkg-type. The pieces inside it are `show sw-component-<location-id>/<swload-state>/<name>` giving state (installed, not-installed, installation-failed, unknown; default unknown), version and description, e.g. `show sw-component-1-5/active/frcu31_ztp_pkg`, and one level down `show sw-subcomponent-<location-id>/<swload-state>/<sw-component-name>/<sw-subcomponent-name>`. The bundled firmware is `show packaged-fw-<location-id>/<swload-state>/<equipment-type>/<fw-name>` with `fw-version`; versions for the same firmware can differ per equipment-type. `swversion` lists active, inactive and installable versions.

Work per port with three show commands. `show lldp-local-info-<lldp-port>` is what this node advertises: chassis-id-subtype chassis-component with the chassis serial number as chassis-id, port-id-subtype local with the port AID as port-id, port-description (the port name), system-name (the NE name) and system-description. `show lldp-neighbor-<lldp-port>/<direction>` is what was received; direction is ingress only, the egress direction is not supported. It gives last-update, age, ttl, chassis-id, port-id, system-name and capabilities, and is kept indefinitely until the port is decommissioned or cleared. `show lldp-port-statistics-<lldp-port>/ingress` separates sending from receiving: total-frames-out, total-frames-in, error-frames, total-discarded-frames, total-discarded-tlvs, total-unrecognized-tlvs, total-ageouts, last-change-time, last-clear-time, all defaulting to 0. These counters freeze whenever lldp-admin-status is disabled for that port. `show lldp hold-on-timer` is the global neighbour retention time, default 900 seconds, used when the neighbour sends no TTL TLV.

`show slot` (or `show slot-<chassis-name>-<slot-name>`, e.g. `show slot-1-1`) lists every holder with AID, `supported-type`, `installed-type`, `oper-state`, `avail-state` and `current-equipment`; an empty installed-type and a current-equipment of --- mean nothing is fitted. `show inventory-<chassis-name>-<slot-name>` gives the FRU data for whatever is in it: hardware-version, actual-type, actual-subtype, sw-support-revision, PON, serial-number, clei, vendor, part-number, manufacture-date, insertion-date, actual-power-class, actual-max-power-draw, and `fw-status` (not-applicable, current, not-current, unavailable; default not-applicable). Firmware level is `show current-fw-<chassis-name>-<slot-name>/<fw-name>` (also addressable per card and per port), returning `fw-version`, `expected-fw-version` and `fw-status` (current, not-current, unavailable; default unavailable). A bare `show current-fw` prints the whole table, e.g. current-fw-1-1/CORE_BOOT 0x20 vs expected 0x28, not-current.

`show manifest-<manifest-file>` lists the downloaded manifest with `manifest-signature` (hex string up to 1024), `downloaded-on` (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ) and `information`. Contents are `show manifest-component-<manifest-file>/<equipment-type>/<name>`, which returns `state` (installed, not-installed, installation-failed, unknown; default unknown), `version` and `description`, so that is where you see whether each piece got installed. Bundled firmware is `show manifest-firmware-<manifest-file>/<equipment-type>/<fw-name>` with `fw-version`. `show downloaded-image-<manifest-file>/<name>` shows the image files pulled down and their `signature`, and `show fru-info-<manifest-file>/<equipment-type>` shows the packaged FRU information for one equipment-type. Example: `show manifest-G40_BASIC-R6.1.0-F-2023.01.04_15_40-x-sim-u-1940.manifest`. For what actually landed on a card, cross-check `show sw-component-<location-id>/<swload-state>/<name>` and `show upgrade-status`.

Two profile objects keyed by resource type. Alarm severity comes from `alarm-severity-entry-<resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location>`, whose `severity` is critical, event, major, minor, not-reported or warning, e.g. `set alarm-severity-entry-tom/EQPTCOMFAIL severity major`; direction is na, ingress or egress and location is na, near-end or far-end. `alarm-severity-profile` is the system-managed container over those entries: `set alarm-severity-profile <profile-entry> severity <value>`. PM defaults come from `pm-profile-entry-<resource-type>/<direction>/<location>/<period>`, whose `default-data-supervision` and `default-tca-supervision` (true/false) state, verbatim, whether newly created resources of this type have PM data supervision and PM threshold crossing supervision automatically enabled. Above it `pm-profile global-data-supervision` is auto-enabled or manual (default manual), and threshold defaults live in `pm-threshold-profile` as `default-low-threshold` and `default-high-threshold`.

`ipsec-spd-entry-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>` is the decision: its `action` is protect, bypass or discard, default protect. `priority` (uint8) is mandatory on add and gives precedence between SPD entries; `mode` is tunnel or transport (default tunnel), `ipsec-protocol` is ESP, `esn` defaults true, `anti-replay-window` is 32..1024 default 64 and applies when action is protect, and `dynamic-ts` defaults disabled. Example: `add ipsec-spd-entry-ipsec/GX2/dns priority 1 action protect`. Underneath the SPD entry hang `ipsec-sa-proposal-.../<number>` and `ipsec-traffic-selector-.../<ipsec-traffic-selector-name>` (with `next-layer-protocol`: any = 0, opaque = 255, or 0-255, default any). Under the traffic selector hang `local-subnet`, `remote-subnet`, `local-ports` and `remote-ports`. `ipsec-sa-re-key` sits under the peer, and `security-policy-database-<ikev2-local-instance>/<ikev2-peer-name>` lists the associated-secure-entity.

`trusted-certificate-<id>` is the CA you trust: the X509v3 CA (Root and Intermediate) certificate trusted by the system. `local-certificate-<id>` is this node's own identity: the X.509v3 end-entity certificate representing one of the various secure application identities; it uniquely carries `used-by` (the secure-applications, ikev2-peers and so on presently using it) and `self-signed`. `peer-certificate-<id>` is the far end: the X509v3 end-entity certificate representing a trusted remote peer certificate for the L1 encryption secure application; it uniquely carries `white-listed`, true when it has no trust chain and was explicitly white-listed at import. The fourth, `certificate`, is not a per-certificate object at all but the operational command over all three: `show certificates`, `show certificate-revocation` and `clear [-f] certificate [type=]<trusted|local|peer> [id=]<value>`. All three share version v3, serial-number, subject-name, issuer, trust-chain, valid-from, valid-to, status and `revocation-mode` (auto, force-revoked, force-unrevoked; default auto).

Import with `import-certificate {-i, <certificate type>} [<certificate-name>] <string in PEM format> [<passphrase>]`, Operational mode; the type is local-certificate, trusted-certificate or peer-certificate, e.g. `import-certificate trusted-certificate certificate-name=trusted-cert-1 <string in PEM format>`. `-i` imports any intermediate certificates present in a PEM bundle, or for a single-certificate file the intermediates named by the AIA extension; root certificates must be installed individually. If no certificate-name is given, the name is derived from the topmost certificate issuer /CN plus a numeric suffix, for example trusted-certificate-Nokia-1. A passphrase applies to trusted-certificate, local-certificate and bundles. Remove with `clear [-f] certificate [type=]<trusted|local|peer> [id=]<value>`, Operational mode, which prompts 'Are you sure? [y/n]'; the id must match a currently installed but unused certificate of that type, and <tab> lists the clearable ids. Bulk options are purge-all-invalid, purge-all-unused, purge-all-expired, purge-local-unused and purge-peer-unused.

`ace-<name>/<sequence-id>` is what permits or blocks IP traffic: its `action` is drop, accept or reject (default drop), matched on source/destination IP, L4 port ranges, `protocol` (default any), `ttl` (1..255, default 255) and `direction` (input or output, default input). Its `sequence-id` sets the relative order within the ACL. `acl-<name>` is the container that binds those entries to an interface (1-AUX-1, 1-AUX-2, DCN, DCN-B, DCN-2, DCN-2-B) with `type` IPv4 or IPv6; an ACL must exist before an ACE can be added. `access-rule-<access-rule-list-name>/<access-rule-name>` is not traffic filtering at all: it permits or denies management access to YANG paths, RPCs and notifications (`action` permit or deny, mandatory), while `access-rule-list-<name>` groups those rules per user-group and is processed in order by `sequence-id`. `access-control-list` is a show-only container. Further out, `sw-control-rule-<service-name>` has nothing to do with access or traffic: its `fail-action` (default-action, ignore, system-restart) governs what happens when a software service fails.

Order is by `sequence-id` (uint16) on `access-rule-<access-rule-list-name>/<access-rule-name>`: lower number ids are processed first, so the lower sequence-id wins. If sequence-id is not provided, it is set to the currently used latest id plus 1, which places the rule at the end of the list. The id can be changed over the lifetime of the access-rule-list to re-sort entries. The list itself, `access-rule-list-<name>`, is a group of access-rules organised by which user-groups they apply to and is likewise processed in order by its own `sequence-id`. Its `user-group` is a leaf-list of user-group names with a maximum of 20 user-groups referenced; the default value '*' is the match-all representation, meaning the list applies to all existing user-groups. The system supports a maximum of 500 access-rules across all access-rule-lists. For IP filtering with `ace`, the sequence-id range is 1-100 for AUX and DCN-B interfaces and 1-256 for DCN-A, recommended in multiples of 5, with a maximum of 16 ACEs per ACL when both upper-port and lower-port are specified.

The trap community string is not on `snmp-community` at all; that object explicitly notes that the trap-community-string is located in the snmp-target object. Set it with `add snmp-target-<target-name> snmpv3-user <value> target-address <value> [enabled <value>] [snmp-version <value>] [trap-community-string <value>] [target-port <value>] [target-transport <value>]` or with `set snmp-target-<target-name> trap-community-string <value>`. `trap-community-string` is a string of 0..32 characters and defaults to 'infinera', which is what a receiver expecting your own string will reject. `snmp-version` is v2c (default) or v3, `snmpv3-user` applies only when the version is v3, `target-port` is 0..65535 default 162, `target-transport` is udp, and `enabled` defaults true. `snmp-community-<name>` with its `community-string` (1..32) and `community-string-access` (read-only) governs polling access only.

`external-fiber-connection-<name>` is the one filled in by something else: the guide states it is set autonomously by TNMS, and although it is possible to configure it manually, it is not recommended to do so. It represents the physical link between two ports of L0 cards in different NEs, or in the same NE in disaggregated configurations, and takes `src-node-id`, `src-card-name`, `src-port-name`, `dst-node-id`, `dst-card-name`, `dst-port-name`, `fiber-connection-type` (one-way or two-way, default two-way) and `scope` (general-purpose or cable-id, default general-purpose; entries not scoped cable-id are excluded from the CableID path and are not verified). By contrast `fiber-connection-<name>` is the user-created intra-NE link between two distinct ports or sub-ports in the same NE, with label, src-port, dst-port and fiber-connection-type. `supporting-fiber-connection-<name>` is show-only and just returns the `fiber-connection-list` supporting an entity.

The one you want is `ipv4-address`: `add ipv4-address-<if-name>/<ip> netmask <value>`, for example `add ipv4-address-DCN-B/10.220.192.213 netmask 255.255.252.0`. `show` adds `origin` (static, dhcp, auto-config; default static). Addresses beginning with 0, with 127, or with 224 up to 255 are disallowed, and only valid netmasks are accepted. The two look-alikes are LLDP read-only objects, not configuration. `management-address-<lldp-port>/<direction>/<address-subtype>/<address>` retrieves the management addresses advertised by the remote system and received on a local port, with `if-subtype` (unknown, if-index, system-port-number), `if-id` and `address-oid`. `management-address-local-<lldp-port>/<address-subtype>/<address>` is the same information for the local LLDP ports, with no direction key, and its `address-oid` is currently an empty string. Neither assigns an address to an interface.

The stated pre-condition on `ipv4-address` is that a static IPv4 address cannot be configured when DHCP is enabled on the interface. So check `show interface-<if-name> ipv4-address-assignment-method`, which is static or dhcp (default static), and `ipv4-enabled` (true/false, default true); switch it back with `set interface-<if-name> ipv4-address-assignment-method static`. The other rejections come from the address itself: addresses beginning with 0 (current network), with 127 (loopback), or with 224 up to 255 (broadcast, multicast and experimental) are disallowed, and only valid netmasks are allowed. To see which interfaces are available, use `show interface` (which returns if-type ethernet, software-loopback, point-to-point, ppp or hdlc, supporting-port, backup-port, vrf, protection-mode and admin/oper/avail-state), or type '?' after `ipv4-address-` and the system displays the object completion options.

`show route-<rib-name>/<destination-prefix>` is the list of system routes from various sources such as dynamic protocols and static routes; `source-protocol` names the origin (OSPF, BGP, static and so on) and `special-next-hop` is none, blackhole or unreachable (default none). The table it lives in is `show rib-<rib-name>`, with `vrf` and `address-family` (ipv4-unicast or ipv6-unicast); for each routing instance the system provides one system-controlled default RIB per supported address family, e.g. `show rib-IPv4`. `show next-hop-<rib-name>/<destination-prefix>/<interface>` gives the `next-hop-address`, e.g. `show next-hop-IPv4/0.0.0.0/0/DCN`. Hand-typed routes are added with `add ipv4-static-route-<ipv4-destination-prefix>/<vrf> [next-hop-address <value>] [advertised <value>] [distance <value>] [interface <value>] [origin <value>] [special-next-hop <value>]`, where `distance` is 1..255 default 1, `advertised` defaults false, and `origin` is manual or dhcp (default manual). Example: `add ipv4-static-route-10.220.0.0/16/MGMT next-hop-address 10.220.225.165`. `ipv6-static-route` is the IPv6 equivalent.

`local-ports` and `remote-ports` are the IPsec pair. Both are keyed `<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<ipsec-traffic-selector-name>/<start>/<stop>`, so they hang under an `ipsec-traffic-selector` inside an `ipsec-spd-entry` on an IKEv2 peer, and they define the local and remote Layer 4 port ranges the selector matches. `start` is all, opaque or a port number; `stop` defaults to 0, and 0 is only accepted when start is all or opaque. Examples: `add local-ports-ipsec/GX1/dns/ts1/53/53` and `add remote-ports-ipsec/GX2/protect1/ts1/all`. `connection-ports` is unrelated to security: `show connection-ports-<degree-number>/<index> [port-name]` is a Layer 0 topology object that reports the dwdm-line port of the RD or ILAx card associated with a degree, and creates the OMS of the corresponding dwdm-port. `degree-number` is 1..20 and must not exceed max-degrees; `index` has range 1..2 but is always 1 in the 1830 GX since dwdm-line ports are bi-directional, e.g. `connection-ports-5/1  port-name port-4-1-dwdm-line1`.

`take-snapshot [[db-passphrase=]<value>] [[db-instance=]<value>] [[description=]<value>]` (Operational mode) creates the local snapshot, storing the current Configuration database into one of the backup slots. `db-instance` is temp (default, temporary storage for manual backup and restore), manual (permanent storage for important configurations), rollback, or the automatic onehour, oneday and oneweek; `type` is db-backup (default) or system-backup; `description` is up to 128 characters. It is refused if the db-passphrase used for snapshot encryption is not configured, either globally via `set security-policies db-passphrase` or as a parameter of this command; the passphrase needs a minimum of 40 characters, must not contain dictionary words, and allows special characters from the 85-character Z85 set. `activate-snapshot db-instance <string> db-paraphrase <string> [sanity-check-override <true|false>]` puts it back, default sanity-check-override false, with the pre-condition that a snapshot must have been taken. `show database` and `show database-<database-type>` (active, manual, oneday, onehour, oneweek, rollback, temp) list them with backup-time, ne-name and description.

activate is one operational-mode verb with several sub-parameters: activate swimage (activates the installable image; implies a system restart; db-action auto|empty-db|upgrade-db|rollback, default auto), activate database (activates the currently inactive database; restart-type cold|warm, default cold; sanity-check-override false/true, default false), activate activate-file, activate location-led (entity = chassis or card, led-mode flash|solid default flash, timeout 0..120 s default 0), activate loopback (WSS loopback on an NMC), activate eqpt-fw (resource plus fw-image-name), activate krp (installs a Key Replacement Package), activate otdr and activate otdr-fiber-check. For the database snapshot case there is a separate command: activate-snapshot db-instance <string> db-paraphrase <string> [sanity-check-override <true|false>], pre-condition being that a snapshot must already have been taken with take-snapshot.

capabilities is the per-card one: show capabilities-<name>, where name is the card name, available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. l0-capabilities is the photonic one: show l0-capabilities shows the capability details related to the node's Layer 0 functions; it takes no parameters. oadm-capabilities is the add/drop one: show oadm-capabilities [max-degrees] [max-adgs], where max-degrees is the maximum number of degrees (20, uint8; 0 if not supported, and 0 by convention for ILA node-type which has only 2 fixed directions) and max-adgs is the maximum number of Add/Drop Groups (110, uint8; 0 if not supported). Degrees and ADGs are only supported on OADM node types.

Use show controller-card-<name> for just the controller: it reports redundancy-status (active, standby, not-in-service; default not-in-service), redundancy-standby-status (ready-synchronized, not-ready-synchronizing, not-ready-synchronize-fail, lock-out, card-not-present; default not-ready-synchronizing), number-of-switchover-events (uint32) and time-of-last-switchover (both visible only on the active controller), and additional-details (string 0..128). Use card (add/set/show/delete card-<name>) for any provisioned card in the shelf: required-type, required-subtype, card-mode, category, chassis-name, slot-name, power-profile, last-reboot-reason, admin-state and so on. Use show supported-card-<card-type> for what a model supports: category, card-width, card-height, max-power-draw, grid-mode-support, supported-card-mode, support-serdes-config, location-led-support, supported-bands, supported-features.

macsec-entity is the Ethernet MACsec one: add/set/show/delete macsec-entity-<name> with supporting-facility (an ethernet facility), enabled (default true), link-security-control must-secure|should-secure (default must-secure), replay-protection enable|disable, replay-protection-window 0..4294967295 (default 0), and a read-only negotiated-cipher-suite. secure-entity is the optical/L1 one: add secure-entity-<name> supporting-facility <value> remote-secure-entity <value>, where remote-secure-entity is the remote optical-carrier (G40), remote ODU (G30) or remote OTUFlex; enabled default false, re-key-frequency 3600..86400 s default 28800, re-key-fail-policy kill-traffic|continue-traffic default continue-traffic, traffic-kill-offset 0..86400 s default 0. Cipher terms live outside both: for MACsec in mka-policy (macsec-cipher-suite, confidentiality-offset), and for the optical side in secure-entity-sa-proposal, which shows encryption-algorithm aes-gcm-16, encryption-key-length key-length-256, integrity-algorithm none and dh-group ecp-521.

ase-idler-service is the Layer 0 service that fills unused and nmc-failed portions of the band spectrum with ASE. It supports add/delete/set/show; ase-idler-enable is enabled|disabled (default disabled), ase-idler-state shows ase-enabled, ase-partially-enabled, ase-faulted or ase-disabled (default ase-disabled), function is idler, alarm-report-control allowed|inhibited default allowed. ase-idler-source is the physical ASE pump feeding it: set/show only, with pump-enable enabled|disabled (default disabled), pump-state, target-output-power range -3.00..20.50 dBm default 13, admin-state lock|unlock|maintenance default unlock, and function ase-idler-source. sw-service does not belong with them at all: it is a software command, show sw-service-<sv-name> / show sw-services, listing OS services and containers on the node with state off|ok|fail, cpu-usage, memory-usage, uptime, last-start-time and reboot-count.

No, they are not harmless. change-ztp-mode [-f] [ztp-mode=]<enabled|disabled> is an operational-mode command: change-ztp-mode enabled starts ZTP, reverts the database to the factory default and triggers a system reboot; change-ztp-mode disabled stops ZTP, including one already in progress. Use show ztp to read the current mode. clear [-f] recover-mode clears the recover-mode flag, confirming the current configuration as is, re-enabling communication with the line cards and potentially reconfiguring the traffic settings, so it may be traffic impacting; it takes no parameters and prompts for confirmation unless -f is given. The carrier-mode commands are the harmless ones: golden-carrier-mode, supported-carrier-mode and gcmt are all show-only retrieval commands for carrier-mode tables (capacity, client-mode, baud-rate, application, compatibility-id, status).

State: show third-party-app-<app-name> reports state running|stopped|failed (default stopped), plus version, vendor, product, label, information and enable (true/false, default false; when enabled the app is started and also restarts on system restart). show third-party-app-info-<location-id>/<app-name> gives per-location version, state and information. Firmware side: show third-party-fw-<fw-name> gives file-status valid|invalid|missing, path, version, crc, vendor, part-number, nsa-upgrade-version, present-in-eqpt and applicable-eqpt (max 80 elements each). Clearing: clear [-f] app [app-name=]<value> clears third-party apps. To control rather than clear one, use appctl [app-name=] [command=] with command restart, netls or exec, target defaulting to system, and up to 50 optional parameters.

Per-session is cli-session-config: set cli-session-config-<session-id> cli-lines <value> changes rows for that login only. cli-lines range is 10..1000, default 40; cli-columns 80..4000, default 80; interactive-mode true/false default true (set per session, not persistent); display-timestamp true/false default false. The protocol as a whole is cli: set/show cli with enabled (default true; CLI cannot be disabled from within a CLI session), port 1..65535 default 22, script-dir, default-interactive-mode (default true, affects only newly created sessions), and show-alarm-columns (default default-columns, global effect on all CLI sessions). The two system-configuration objects are config (show config [<entity-id>|<entity-type>], showing non-default configuration recursively from the current scope) and extended-config (add/delete/show extended-config-<name>, a non-standard global exception whose name must match one known by the system).

set is the generic attribute assignment: set [-f|-v] [<entity id>] <attribute> <value> ... [<filter> ...], valid in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode, supporting wildcards (card-*, port-1-4-*), ranges card-1-[1..4] and lists interface-[DCN,CRAFT]; it asks for confirmation when the request may be traffic impacting or implicitly affects multiple instances. set-alarm-state is the alarm-state operation: set-alarm-state [state=]<value> [[acknowledge-text=]<value>] (all-alarms | [alarm-id-list=]<value>...), states none, ack and close, alarm-id-list taking 1 to 10 alarm ids, acknowledge-text a string 0..256. set-time is the time operation: set-time [new-time=]<value> in ISO 8601 form 2017-01-12T10:22:25Z or with +/-hh:mm, only applicable when time-source is manual (NTP not enabled). The one ending in -set is named-value-set: add/set/delete/show named-value-set-<db-entry-name>/<named-value-set-name> [value], value being a string 1..1024 characters.

mc is the Media Channel: add mc-<name> parent-oms <value> lower-frequency <value> upper-frequency <value>, frequencies in MHz, with center-frequency and slot-width calculated by the system, and auto-delete disabled|enabled default disabled (only allowed on RD66TM sleds with l0-mode-op=hsc-ols). nmc is the Network Media Channel, the actual carrier-bearing channel: add nmc-<name> parent-facility <value> center-frequency <value>, where parent-facility can be an MC or an OMS, center-frequency 190650000..196700000 MHz, width 15000..200000 MHz default 35000, plus power and attenuation targets, ASE insertion and loopback state. The fillers are read-only occupancy reporting: mc-f (Media Channel Filler) shows lower-frequency, upper-frequency and slot-width only; nmc-f (Network Media Channel Filler) adds set of admin-state and alarm-report-control plus alloc-/actual- lower and upper frequency, alloc-bandwidth default 75000 MHz, actual-bandwidth default 0, and power-actual-tx/rx.

The scan is run by activate: activate otdr [entity=]<port> [[otdr-file-prefix=]<value>] triggers a measurement on an OTDR port, and activate otdr-fiber-check [entity=]<ots-r-id> triggers a manual OTDR-based fiber check (up to 3 OTDR tests; it errors if a manual scan or automatic Raman fiber check is already in progress). Tuning lives in otdr-ptp: otdr-range auto or 0..300.0 km, otdr-pulse-width auto or 10..20000 ns, otdr-measurement-speed fast|medium|slow|precision|auto|high-precision (default auto), otdr-ior auto or 1.0..2.0, otdr-fiber-type (default auto), otdr-resolution auto or 0.4..100.0, otdr-direction-mode default counter-prop-in-service, peak-power auto or 5..14.5, launching-fiber-length 0..50 m default 0. Results come out on otdr-ptp as otdr-fiber-break-distance (km, or not-available), otdr-last-measurement and otdr-last-measurement-file (.sor). Live status is on otdr: otdr-state not-available|idle|measuring|finished|fail, otdr-measurement-time, otdr-measurement-direction and otdr-error.

The name server entry comes back because of origin. dns-server-<address> has an origin attribute of dhcp (address assigned to this system by a DHCP server) or manual (default manual); a DHCP-learned entry is re-supplied unless you convert it by setting origin to manual. The global gate is dns assignment-method, which is manual, dhcp or both (default both), alongside enabled (default true) and search (a DNS search suffix that must contain at least one dot). For the relay, there are two levels: global dhcp-relay with mode disabled|ipv4|ipv6 (default disabled) and server-address (at least one IP must be configured when enabled), and per-interface if-dhcp-relay-<if-name> with dhcp-relay-enabled true/false, default false, which obeys the global dhcp-relay settings. A relay does nothing if either the global mode is disabled or the interface flag is left at false.

clear [-f] system [type=]<value> [[target=]<value>] [[restart-behavior=]<value>] does a secure wipe with three types. factory-reset resets the system or a particular equipment to factory configuration, stopping target traffic services and removing respective files and user configurations; it does not take effect for G30 Optical Carrier-Cards (OCC2T, OCC2E) but is supported on the G30 controller card (FRCU). full-wipe cleans the entire system and reinstalls SW on the controller and line cards, removing all files, configurations and software, and requires a base software reinstall from ONIE to recover. inactive just clears the inactive software partition. target may be the whole system (the default if omitted) or a chassis/card AID; restart-behavior is restart (default) or shutdown, and factory-reset with shutdown is not supported on L0 cards. The option that leaves logs and PM behind is clear [-f] database (clear-type full, keep-networking or initialize-from-script, default full): it sets the NE database to default and reboots, but explicitly does not wipe logs, PM data or other non-configuration data.

Read show unprovisioned-inventory-<chassis-serial-number>/<slot-name>: it lists inventory detected but not yet accepted by the Node Controller in a multi-chassis configuration, with hardware-version, actual-type, actual-subtype, sw-support-revision, PON, serial-number, clei, vendor, part-number, manufacture-date and detection-timestamp (the last time the Node Controller detected it). Anything appearing there has been seen but not taken in. Cross-check the cabling with show nct-connection-<src-port>/<dst-port>, which shows src-chassis, dst-chassis and src-/dst-chassis-state as node controller, provisioned or unprovisioned; unprovisioned ports appear in the form <chassis-serial-number>-<slot>-NCT-<id>. On the chassis object itself, show chassis-<name> reports is-node-controller, chassis-role (unknown, main-chassis, sub-chassis), expected-serial-number (which is how you tell the NC the serial number of a sub-chassis) and equipment-discovery-ready.

control-mode decides it: auto-max-pw (the default, auto mode targeting maximum output power) means the system sets the gain, manual means you set it. In manual mode gain-target applies, range 0..40 dB, default 0.0; in auto mode gain-adjustment applies as a user offset in the range -20.00..20.00 dB, default 0, and is only supported on amplifiers whose function is pa or inline. amp-control-support reports whether auto-max-pw is even configurable (auto vs manual-only). Setting control-mode to manual automatically sets gain-range-control to manual, and auto-max-pw sets it to auto. Things that stop output entirely: amplifier-enable disabled (the default) so no output power at all; forced-shutdown true on dual-band cards; admin-state lock; and for the underlying dependency, output power needs the OSC signal on an ILA node, or OMS facilities plus an OXcon on an OADM node. On input OLOS the amplifier shuts down after olos-shutdown-soak-timer (0..2000 ms, default 0) unless olos-shutdown-disable is true.

The live member is shown by protection-unit: show protection-unit-<protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name> reports state (active, standby, available, unknown) and role (working or protection), plus transport-entity and AID. On the group, show protection-group-<name> pg-state gives the overall condition (no-request, forced-to-working, sf-on-working, wait-to-restore, unavailable and so on) and last-switch-trigger the reason for the last switchover. Behaviour is set on protection-group: protection-type y-cable or snc-n (default y-cable), switching-mode unidirectional or bidirectional (default unidirectional), reversion-mode revertive or non-revertive (default non-revertive), hold-off-timer 0..10000 ms in 1 ms steps (default 0), wtr-timer 60..720 s (default 300, revertive only) with remaining-wtr, pg-request (clear, manual-to-working/protection, forced-to-working/protection, protection-lockout, exercise), pg-control-request freeze/clear-freeze, and the trigger switches client-side-olos-trigger, client-side-sd-trigger, network-side-csf-trigger, network-side-sd-trigger (all default disabled). Manual switching is done with protection-switch operation-type force|lockout|manual|release.

Trigger the check with verify [-f] fiber-connection [target-select=]<port-id> [allow-switching]. If no port-id is given, all paths are verified; allow-switching is false by default, meaning only active paths are checked, and true lets the system initiate OPSM switching so both active and inactive paths are verified. The pre-condition is that equipment-policies cable-id-control is set to enabled; when accepted the system raises CID-verification-in-progress against the NE and replies that verification has started. Watch progress with show cable-id-status: cable-id-state is idle, running-incl-switching or running-no-switching, and test-progress is a string of the form 'N out of M completed'. Per-pair results are in show cable-id-path-<name>: port-a-to-port-z-last-test-status and port-z-to-port-a-last-test-status (not-verified, pass, fail), path-status enabled/disabled, last-test-qualifier up-to-date/out-dated, last-test-timestamp and additional-info (Cable-ID TxLOS, RxLOS, Cable-ID-MISMATCH, RxLOF, Power out-of-range, timeout). show -r adds the supporting fiber connections. terminate cable-id stops running tests.

Where authentication is sent is aaa-server: add/set aaa-server-<server-name> protocol-supported RADIUS|TACACSPLUS (default RADIUS), server-address, server-priority 1..10 (lower number is higher precedence; if omitted the new server gets the lowest precedence in use plus 1), server-port default 49, server-port-authentication default 1812, server-port-accounting default 1813, shared-secret (max 64 characters accepted, default sharedkey), source-ip (source IP used for RADIUS communications), role-supported authentication/authorization/accounting, and enabled default true. What happens when the box does not answer is governed by timeout, 1..90 seconds default 5, and retry, 0..5 default 1, with the total wait time timeout x (retry + 1) required to be under 5 minutes, plus security-policies aaa-authentication-method: local-only (the default), local-first-then-remote, remote-first-then-local, or remote-unavailable-then-local. Authorization fallback is set separately by security-policies aaa-authorization-method.

For the automation account use ssh-authorized-key: add ssh-authorized-key-<user-name>/<key-id> public-key <value> [label], one trusted public key per entry for SSHv2 user authentication; user-name may be a local or remote user, key-id is a string 1..64, public-key is up to 2048 characters in OpenSSH/PEM form, and public-key-algorithm is reported as ecdsa-sha2-nistp256/384/521 or ssh-rsa2048/3072/4096. Also set security-policies ssh-authentication-method to public-key or public-key-or-password (default is password). For the remote host the node copies files to, use ssh-known-host: add ssh-known-host-<id> address <value> public-key-algorithm <value> public-key <value>, where address is a hostname/IPv4/IPv6 and the algorithm may additionally be ssh-ed25519 (from R9.0); enforcement is by security-policies ssh-strict-host-key-checking, strict or relaxed (default relaxed). The node's own identity is ssh-host-key (show only, one per algorithm, with fingerprint md5 or sha256), generated or replaced by ssh-keygen [-b=<length>] [-l=<label>] [-t=<rsa|ecdsa|ed25519>], default type rsa.

The key agreement policy lives in mka-policy: add/set/show/delete mka-policy-<name> with key-server-priority (used by MKA to select the key server), macsec-cipher-suite for Secure Association Key derivation, confidentiality-offset (the number of octets in an Ethernet frame sent as unencrypted plain text), and sak-rekey-interval. Session key rollover is that sak-rekey-interval, in seconds, range 0 or 30..65535, default 30 s. The policy is bound to the port through macsec-mka-<name>, which carries mka-policy (the policy name to use), is-key-server (default false), connectivity-association-key and connectivity-association-key-name (strings 0..64), psk-lifetime in days range 1..173 default 14, psk-expiration-warning, psk-lifetime-enable and psk-configured-timestamp. Watch the channels with show sc-tx-<name>/<index> and show sc-rx-<name>/<index>: each gives sci-tx / sci-rx (16-character hex string), state in-use or not-in-use, association-number, key-identifier and next-packet-number. The port-level object is macsec-entity, which also reports negotiated-cipher-suite.

NETCONF listens on port 830 via ssh, enabled true by default (it cannot be disabled from within a NETCONF session), with hello-timeout 1..3600 seconds default 2, annotate-cli-name default false, and static-info-in-notifs up to 10 YANG identifiers. gNMI/gRPC listens on port 50051, enabled true by default, with gnmi-get-encoding-granularity per-path or per-object, default per-object; the grpc object is system managed and cannot be manually deleted. Nothing on those two is off out of the box. The one partly off by default is RESTCONF: enabled is true and https-enabled is true on port 8181, but http-enabled is false by default on port 8080, and RESTCONF HTTP access is not supported in secure mode. RESTCONF cookie-timeout is 1..300 minutes, default 5. All three port fields accept 1..65535.

restart [-h] [-f] [<resource-id>] [<type>] [<sub-component>] defaults to a warm restart if no type is given, and restarts the active node controller if no resource-id is given; it prompts for confirmation unless -f is used. warm reboots the processor of the card and is non-service affecting, with connectivity regained within five minutes (on XMM4 it is non-service affecting but visibility is lost for 3 minutes). cold reboots all components and sub-components and is service affecting, again with connectivity back within five minutes; cold reboot of XMM4 is not service affecting though visibility is lost, while cold reboot of CHM6, UCM4 and similar is service affecting. shutdown gracefully shuts the card down. No, you cannot assume uniformity: the guide states explicitly that not all cards support all restart types. Restartable entities are card (cold, warm, shutdown), card sub-component (cold, warm) and tom (cold only); list sub-components with show card resources.

Three things must be in place. First, a serdes-template per TOM part number: add serdes-template-<name> [tom-part-number <value>] [card-types-applicable <value>] [ports-applicable <value>], where tom-part-number is a string 1..16 and ports-applicable is 'all' (the default behaviour, all ports considered) or up to 20 port names. Second, the actual parameter values as serdes-template-entry-<serdes-template-name>/<serdes-template-entry-name> value <value>, for example RxAmplitude, RxEQ, TxEQ, RxPreCursor, TxEQAdaptive. Third, the global flag: set equipment-templates use-serdes-templates enabled, which defaults to disabled; application of serdes-templates depends on this flag being true. Templates then apply automatically to all line cards that support serdes when a TOM with that part-number is plugged in. Manual serdes configuration is still kept even where it deviates from the template; swapping in a TOM with a different part-number resets serdes and re-applies the new template. Enabling the flag does not retro-apply, so force re-application with apply-template serdes-template [applicable-tom=]<list>.

ots is the Optical Transport Section, the fibre span itself: fiber-type-tx/rx (default SSMF), fiber-length-tx/rx auto or 0..500.0 km, span-loss-transmit/receive 0..80 dB, span-loss-reference configured or measured (default measured), external-attenuation-tx/rx 0..30 dB, target-power-setting manual|auto|auto-plan (default auto), and laser-safety-mode OPLM or APSD. oms is the Optical Multiplex Section, the multiplexed spectrum on top of it: monitoring-mode (intrusive, non-intrusive, not-monitored, dge-fixed-attenuation, ila-with-equalization, integrated-equalization), grid-mode flexible (default) or fixed-50G-96ch, fixed-100G-48ch, fixed-75G-64ch, fixed-75G-64ch-oif, fixed-50G-7100, fixed-150G-40ch, lower-frequency 191300000 and upper-frequency 196150000 MHz, and attenuation-control-mode-rx/tx. ops is the Optical Physical Section on add/drop and other ports: role tributary, multi-carrier, general-purpose (default), ase-input or active-multi-carrier, input-psd-profile -30..-6 dBm/12.5GHz default -6, port-expansion no or y-cable. osc carries the supervisory traffic: osc-mode OC3 (155 Mbit/s) or 1GE for HSC OLS, l0-comm-interface-type ipv4 or ipv6, osc-control auto (default) or manual, target-output-power -2.5..4.5 dBm, tx-power-adjustment -6..6 dB, voa-attenuation-target-rx 0..30 dB default 10, and lof-soak-timer short or long.

The behaviour is configured on trib-ptp with tributary-disable-action, which says what the NE does towards the client equipment connected over the TOM when a line-side failure is observed. The default is laser-shut-off, so by default the node turns the client laser off. The other permitted values are none, odu-ais, send-ais-1, send-gais, send-idles, send-lf, send-ms-ais, and send-nos (G30 only), which insert a replacement signal instead of shutting the laser. Timing is set by tributary-disable-holdoff-timer, uint16 range 0..10000 milliseconds, default 0 meaning holdoff disabled; it applies only when the TDA action is laser-shut-off, holding the optical signal as it is until the timer expires before turning the laser off. Related switches on the same object are near-end-tda (enabled/disabled, default disabled), tda-degrade-mode (enabled/disabled, default disabled, for BERSD-ODU triggering ALS) and forward-defect-trigger (true/false, default true), which decides whether a received client forward defect such as LF or ODU-AIS flows through to the line side or triggers an egress TDA action. Example: set trib-ptp-1-5-T2 tributary-disable-action laser-shut-off.

Every facility carries `managed-by` (system|user, default system); only user-created facilities can be user-deleted. Created for you: line-ptp, trib-ptp and flexo default to managed-by system, and the odu page states "The high order ODU is automatically created when an SCH is created". You add by hand: the super-channel (`add super-channel-<name> carriers <v> carrier-mode <v>`), then low-order ODUs (`add odu-<name> odu-type ODU4i|ODUflexi|ODU4|ODUflex parent-odu <HO-ODU> time-slots <1..255>`), the line OTU (`add otu-1-5-L1-1-OTU4-1 parent flexo-group-1-5-L1-1 time-slots 1`) and the xcon. The stated pre-condition is: "Super-channel must be added before Low Order ODUs can be added." Check what exists with `show facilities` and `show odu`.

BERT: `bert start test-id=TestX resource=ethernet-1-6-T1 test-signal-type=scrambled-idles test-signal-monitoring-type=scrambled-idles test-signal-direction=ingress test-signal-monitoring-direction=egress test-duration=10` (Operational Mode). test-signal-type none|PRBS31|PRBS31NONINV|scrambled-idles (default none); monitoring-type adds fec-frames; test-duration min 10 s, max 1000 hrs, 0 = indefinite. Then `bert stop test-id=TestX` (test-id mandatory), `bert get`, `bert delete`. Test pattern injection also lives on `set odu-diagnostics-<name>/<direction> test-signal-type` (none|PRBS31Q|PRBS13Q|scrambled-idles|PRBS9|PRBS31|PRBS31NONINV, default none), test-signal-direction ingress|egress|both (default ingress), test-signal-monitoring true|false (default false). Loopback: `set otu-<name> loopback none|facility|terminal` (default none) with loopback-mode loopback|loopback-and-continue; optical-carrier also has loopback none|facility|terminal.

The facility must exist and be named as the supporting-facility, and the far end must be identified: `add secure-entity-<name> supporting-facility <facility> remote-secure-entity <AID> enabled true`. remote-secure-entity is the AID of the remote optical carrier (1830 GX G40), the remote ODU (G30), or the remote OTUflex for CHM7/CHM7X L1 service encryption. enabled defaults to false, alarm-report-control defaults to inhibited, re-key-frequency 3600..86400 s (default 28800), re-key-fail-policy kill-traffic|continue-traffic (default continue-traffic), traffic-kill-offset 0..86400 s (default 0). Certificates must be in place at each end: a local-certificate as the node's identity plus a peer-certificate, which "represents a trusted 'remote peer' certificate for L1 encryption secure application", loaded with `import-certificate`. Verify with `show data-path-encryption` and `show secure-entity-<name> oper-state`.

The telemetry object covers persistent and dynamic telemetry: `show telemetry` and `set telemetry id <string>` (0..4096 chars). It is system-managed and cannot be manually deleted. `show subscriptions` lists the subscription set. Per subscription: `show current-subscription-<subscription-name> [related-session-id] [related-dial-out-server] [session-type] [session-protocol] [encoding] [transfer-mode] [updates-only] [user-access]`, where session-type is gnmi-dial-in, gnmi-dial-out-tunnel or gnmi-dial-out-reverse-rpc, session-protocol gnmi, encoding json|bytes|proto|ascii|json-ietf (default json-ietf), transfer-mode stream|once|poll (default stream), updates-only default false. What each one watches: `show subscription-path-<subscription-name>/<subscription-path-name>` giving subscription-path, subscription-path-origin, subscription-path-mode target-defined|on-change|sample (default target-defined), sample-interval and heartbeat-interval in ms (default 0), suppress-redundant (default true).

At rest the database is encrypted: `show db-protection-scheme` reports encryption-algorithm xts-aes-256-plain64 (AES-256 in XTS mode), integrity-algorithm hmac-sha2-512 or none, integrity-status passed-on-bootup|failed-on-bootup|disabled, and mode encryption-only or encryption-with-integrity, changeable via the db-migrate RPC. Before you can take a copy, the db-passphrase must be set: "The system will only accept this command if the db-passphrase (used for DB snapshot encryption) is configured, either in global configuration (as part of the security-policies), or locally as a parameter of this command." So use `set security-policies db-passphrase` (40..200 chars, minimum 40, no dictionary words, Z85 character set) or `take-snapshot db-passphrase=***`. Automatic snapshots stay disabled until it is set. `take-snapshot [db-instance=]<temp|manual|onehour|oneday|oneweek|rollback>` (default temp) with optional description; list results with `show database`.

Start at the RIB: `show rib-<rib-name> [vrf] [address-family]`. Each RIB holds one address family (ipv4-unicast or ipv6-unicast), and for each routing instance the system provides one system-controlled default RIB per supported address family, so the vrf leaf tells you which instance the prefix landed in. Then `show route-<rib-name>/<destination-prefix> [special-next-hop] [source-protocol]`: source-protocol shows whether it came from OSPF, BGP or static, and special-next-hop none|blackhole|unreachable shows if it is deliberately discarded (for blackhole and unreachable no next-hop is created under the route). Resolve the hop with `show next-hop-<rib-name>/<destination-prefix>/<interface> [next-hop-address]`, for example `show next-hop-IPv4/0.0.0.0/0/DCN`. Cross-check the source with `show ipv4-static-route-<prefix>/<vrf>` (distance 1..255, default 1; monitoring-state unmonitored|ok|failed); the interface's VRF must match the static route's vrf. `show routing` and `show vrf-<name>` (type mgmt|internal) give the wider view.

Password rules come from `show security-policies`: strict-password-check (default true) enforces minimum 8 characters plus at least one lowercase, one uppercase, one number and one symbol, and the username cannot be part of the password; disabled drops all of that to a 1-character minimum. minimum-password-length is 1..200, default 8. enforce-password-history-check (default true) blocks reuse of the previous 5 passwords, with password-history-size 1..200, default 5. These only apply to newly defined passwords. Lockout is per user: `show user-<name>` gives user-status (enabled, disabled, password-aged or lockout, where lockout means the account is locked after unsuccessful logins), failed-logins, max-invalid-login 0..255 default 5, and suspension-time 0..1440 minutes default 5. security-policies also has disable-user-lockout. To clear a stuck session run `show session` and then `kill-session <session-id>` with the id in the form <ip-address>:<port>; you cannot kill your own session, and only SA users see all sessions.

Untouched defaults: log-file keeps number-of-files 10 (range 1..20) and rotates at max-file-size 30 MB (range 1..30), source-facilities all, sensitive-data none (only for log-file-default-audit-dbg), and "By default, severity is set to informational and above". The default system log file cannot be edited or deleted. Console logging is off: `log-console enabled` defaults to false. Remote servers default to enabled true, port 514, transport udp, message-format rfc5424, message-coalescence true, origin manual, sensitive-data none, destination-facility-override disabled. Node-wide syslog defaults: source-address localhost, log-file-message-coalescence true, log-relay false, assignment-method both, niap-compliant-logging false, privacy-mode false. The single switch that kills everything remote is `set syslog remote-logging-switch false`: "If false, disable all remote logging destinations" (default true).

What is raised now: `show current-alarms [number-of-alarms] [last-changed]`, and `show alarms` / `show alarm-<alarm-id>` for detail (perceived-severity, service-affecting, reported-time, corrective-action, operator-state). Manual clearing: `clear [-f] alarm [alarm-type=]<value> [[resource=]<value>]`, which only works on the small subset of alarms with no automatic clear criteria; find them with `show alarm-inventory can-be-cleared-by-user=true`. This mechanism applies only to system-wide alarms not associated with a particular resource. `set-alarm-state` changes the operator state of an alarm. Whether inhibiting reporting drops what is already up is decided by `set alarm-control arc-behavior`: clear-alarms means that when ARC is set to inhibit the current alarms are cleared, leave-alarms leaves them raised. The default is leave-alarms. alarm-control also carries alarm-soaking-behavior automatic|no-soak, default automatic.

The Equipment dashboard is the temperature view: `status equipment` walks chassis, cards and TOMs and prints temperature sensors and power values alongside presence, oper-state and alarms, for example "chassis-1 G42 (NC) temp 25C | power 2.1/4400 W" and "card-1-1 XMM4 (Act) temp 25C". To narrow it, give the chassis id as the filter, for example `status equipment 5`; only existing chassis ids are accepted, wildcards are not supported, so it is either all chassis or exactly one. For the raw sensor readings use `show pm`, whose real-time PM per resource gives temperature (C) with instant/avg/min/max, plus fan-speed (percent) per FAN card and chassis inlet-temperature; filter with a resource such as `show pm card-1-7`. Physically the state shows on the LEDs: `show leds`, `show led status` or `show led-<location>/<name> status`, with values off, green, flashing-green, yellow, flashing-yellow, amber, flashing-amber, red, flashing-red, cycling, cycling-with-off, not-available.

The line is the OTS: `show ots-<name>` gives span-loss-derived-rx and span-loss-derived-tx, the measured span loss based on OSC including losses external to the fiber (0..99 dB, where 99 dB means OLOS, and only relevant when an OSC channel exists). Compare against the configured span-loss-transmit and span-loss-receive (0..80 dB, default 0; receive also accepts 99 as not configured, and changing it is traffic affecting). span-loss-reference (configured|measured, default measured) decides which one the system uses to calculate automatic target OXCon powers. span-loss-alarm-threshold (0..80 dB, 99) is set autonomously by the system and persists across reboot; in measured mode force a refresh with `update`. Also useful: span-loss-aging-margin-rx (0..10 dB, default 1.0), external-attenuation-tx/rx (0..30 dB) and fiber-length-derived-rx/tx. The compensation is on the amplifier: `show amplifier-<name>` reports gain-operating and gain-target (0..40 dB), gain-range-actual, gain-adjustment (-20..20 dB), input-power-mon and output-power-mon (-99..99 dBm), tilt-actual, control-state, control-mode auto-max-pw (default) or manual, and span-loss-control (default enabled), which must be enabled when span-loss-reference is measured.

Client side first: trib-ptp is the tributary client physical termination between the transceiver and the protocol layer, carrying the protocol client facility above it (ethernet, otu, fc, stm, eth-zr). That client maps into a mapped or low-order odu, which is joined to the line by an xcon (`add xcon-1 source ethernet-1-4-T1 destination odu-1-4-T1-1-ODUni-1`). On the line side the low-order ODU sits under the high-order ODUCn/ODUCni, which is carried by the line otu (added with `parent flexo-group-...`) and flexo, all supported by line-ptp. The digital domain ends at the optical-carrier / optical-channel under the super-channel and super-channel-group: that is where frequency, tx-power and modulation-format are set. From there the optical domain takes over at the nmc (Network Media Channel), whose parent-facility is a Media Channel or an OMS and which is joined by an oxcon, then oms and ots out to the fiber. Walk it with `show facilities` and each facility's supporting-facilities and supported-facilities.

No, they are two different objects. A counter crossing a limit is PM: `add pm-threshold-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location>/<parameter> [low-threshold <value>] [high-threshold <value>]` (also set/show/delete). Values are numbers (uint64, int64, decimal64), na or not-supported, defaulting to na; direction ingress|egress|all|na and location all|na|near-end|far-end both default to all. The TCA itself is armed with `set pm-control-entry-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location> tca-supervision true|false`, with per-type defaults from `set pm-profile-entry-<resource-type>/<direction>/<location>/<period> default-tca-supervision`. Changing how loudly an existing fault is reported is alarm severity: `set alarm-severity-entry-<resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location> severity <critical|event|major|minor|not-reported|warning>`, for example `set alarm-severity-entry-OTU2/TIM/ingress/near-end severity minor`, or `set alarm-severity-profile <profile-entry> severity <value>`. Both alarm-severity objects are system-managed and cannot be manually deleted.

Inhibit reporting on the card with `set card-<name> alarm-report-control inhibited` (values allowed and inhibited); the same alarm-report-control attribute exists on the facilities underneath (otu, odu, trib-ptp, line-ptp, flexo, ots, nmc, amplifier, super-channel), where the default is allowed. What happens to alarms the card has already raised is decided node-wide by `set alarm-control arc-behavior`: with leave-alarms, which is the default, current alarms stay raised when ARC is set to inhibit; with clear-alarms they are cleared. So set `arc-behavior clear-alarms` first if you want the standing alarms to disappear from the NOC as well. You can also put the card itself out of service with `set card-<name> admin-state maintenance` (lock, unlock or maintenance, default unlock). Confirm the result with `show current-alarms` and `show card-<name> alarm-report-control admin-state`.

A secure-application "represents an application which uses X509v3 certificate as its digital identity". Run `show secure-application-<id> [type] [active-certificate-id] [in-use] [status] [verify-client-cert]`: active-certificate-id is the list of assigned certificates (string 0..128), and in-use is a leafref to active-certificate-id, that is the one actually presented; type is server or client and status is enabled or disabled. Assign with `set secure-application-WebGUI active-certificate-id client`, or several with `set secure-application-gRPC active-certificate-id certX,certY`. verify-client-cert is disabled or required (default disabled) and must be required for TLS Mutual Authentication; changes apply only to new TLS connections. Before it will come up the certificate has to be imported: `import-certificate local-certificate certificate-name=local-cert-1 <string in PEM format> <passphrase>`, plus its CA chain as trusted-certificate (root certificates must be installed individually; -i pulls in intermediates from a bundle). Verify with `show local-certificate-<id>` status (valid, expired, revoked, untrusted, future, pending-import) and used-by.

Pipe the show output through the csv display filter: `show pm <command flag> | display csv`, which is importable to a spreadsheet such as Excel; `display xml` and `display json` are also available. Restrict it to the 15-minute bins with the pm-15min period filter and the parameter, resource, resource-type, AID or data-type pm-filters (use `show pm <tab>` for the full filter list). Bin 0 is the current data and bins 1 to n are history, with the bin-to-timestamp mapping printed alongside. Useful flags: -t for standard table format, -n=<number-of-records> (default 1000 records per chassis), -s=<skip-records> for paging, -st= and -et= for a timestamp window (format 2021-02-01T10:00:00+01:00), -sbin=/-ebin= for a bin window, and -i=<chassis-name> (only once per command).

Use `show pm-catalog <string>`, where the string is the catalog name. For example `show pm-catalog parameter-undersized` returns:  pm-parameter-undersized, units packets, type counter. The same information is available from the parameter object itself with `show pm-parameter-<parameter> [units] [type]`, for example `show pm-parameter-severely-errored-seconds`, or `show pm-parameter` for the full list. Both are available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Turn data supervision off on that resource: `set pm-control <entity> data-supervision false`, for example `set pm-control pm-resource-card-1-1 data-supervision false`. data-supervision is described as real-time data supervision for the resource, takes true or false and defaults to true. The equivalent per-instance switch is `set pm-resource-<resource> real-time-supervision <true|false>`, also defaulting to true; `show pm-resource-<resource>` displays resource-type, AID, real-time-supervision and real-time-data-last-reset. Both commands work in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode, and `show pm-control` lists every resource in the system that supports PM data.

Yes. pm-control-entry configures PM for one particular resource, for one particular period, direction and location, so use `set pm-control-entry-<resource>/pm-15min/ingress/near-end tca-supervision true`, for example `set pm-control-entry-trib-ptp-1-7-T9/pm-15min/ingress/near-end tca-supervision true`. direction accepts ingress, egress, all or na (default all) and location accepts all, na, near-end or far-end (default all), so naming pm-15min/ingress/near-end scopes it exactly to the 15-minute ingress near-end counters of that one resource. The same entry also carries data-supervision (true|false). `show pm-control-entry-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location> [supported-parameters] [data-supervision] [tca-supervision]` lists the PM parameters the resource type supports for that direction and location, up to a maximum of 100 elements.

Ask the parameter object: `show pm-parameter-<parameter> [units] [type]`. type reports either counter or gauge, and units is one of na, dBm, ms, ps, ps/nm, dB, seconds, packets, events, octets, bits, blocks, times, percent, bit-ratio, C, frames, W, V, A, rpm, ps2, mA, words, cw, nm, bytes, errors or MHz. For example `show pm-parameter pm-parameter-undersized` returns units packets and type counter, and `show pm-parameter-severely-errored-seconds` targets a single parameter. `show pm-parameter` on its own lists all PM parameters. The same two fields come back from `show pm-catalog <catalog-name>`.

Yes, through the pm-profile object: `set pm-profile global-data-supervision auto-enabled`. global-data-supervision "provides a way to globally enable PM data-supervision without having to toggle it individually"; auto-enabled turns PM data-supervision on globally, while manual, which is the default, leaves the flag controlled via pm-profile-entry or directly per pm-control-entry. Read it back with `show pm-profile`. The pm-profile holds the information on all resources that support PM data together with their default configuration; it is managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Set the per-resource-type default: `set pm-profile-entry-<resource-type>/<direction>/<location>/<period> default-data-supervision true`. default-data-supervision means "For newly created resources of this type, whether they have PM data supervision automatically enabled or not" (true|false), and the companion default-tca-supervision does the same for threshold crossing supervision. direction takes ingress, egress, all or na (default all), location takes all, na, near-end or far-end (default all), and period is a PM period such as pm-15min or pm-24h. Read it back with `show pm-profile-entry-<resource-type>/<direction>/<location>/<period> [default-data-supervision] [default-tca-supervision]`. Existing instances are still changed per resource with pm-control-entry.

Read the real-time-data-last-reset attribute of the port's pm-resource: `show pm-resource-<resource> real-time-data-last-reset`, for example `show pm-resource-trib-ptp-1-7-T9`. It is a date-and-time giving the last real-time data reset for that resource, and if the data was never reset it is the date and time of the resource's creation. The same show also returns resource-type, AID (string, 1..64 characters) and real-time-supervision (true|false, default true), and lists the pm-control-entry children such as pm-control-entry-trib-ptp-1-7-T9/pm-15min/ingress/near-end. A reset is what `clear pm real-time` performs.

Create a pm-threshold keyed to that instance: `add pm-threshold-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location>/errored-seconds high-threshold <value>`, then adjust with the matching `set`, read with `show` and remove with `delete pm-threshold-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location>/errored-seconds`. direction is ingress, egress, all or na (default all) and location is all, na, near-end or far-end (default all); period is a PM period such as pm-15min or pm-24h. Both low-threshold and high-threshold accept a number (uint64, int64 or decimal64), na for not applicable, or not-supported, and both default to na. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Arm the reporting with tca-supervision on the corresponding pm-control-entry.

Query the pm-threshold-profile, which holds PM configuration per parameter for a resource type: `show pm-threshold-profile-<resource-type>/<direction>/<location>/<period>/<parameter> [low-threshold] [high-threshold] [default-low-threshold] [default-high-threshold] [min-value] [max-value]`. default-low-threshold and default-high-threshold are the system defined default values for that parameter, and min-value and max-value are the minimum and maximum permitted for it; all four are show-only and take a number (uint64, int64, decimal64), na or not-supported. low-threshold and high-threshold are the configured values, settable here, for example `set pm-threshold-profile-OTUC14i/ingress/near-end/pm-24h/errored-seconds high-threshold 1200`. direction defaults to all and location defaults to all.

Use set clock timezone <value> to change the zone, for example set clock timezone Beijing-Chongqing-Hong_Kong-Urumqi[GMT+08:00]. The timezone attribute takes one of the named zones in the guide's list (International Date Line West[GMT-12:00] through Kiritimati[GMT+14:00] plus Universal-Time-Coordinated); the default is Universal-Time-Coordinated. To see where the time comes from, use show clock time-source: ntp means the NE synchronises via NTP, manual means it uses the NE internal clock. The default is manual. show clock also returns current-time, universal-time, timezone, uptime, uptime-seconds, DST-active (true/false, default false) and last-time-jump in the form <time1> to <time2> (jumps under 10 seconds are ignored). Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. If the DNS server is not properly configured, show clock can take up to 2 minutes to respond.

Yes. node-type is set with set ne node-type OADM; permitted values are ILA, OADM and XPDR. It can only be set or changed on a 1830 GX G34c chassis, which defaults to ILA (G31/G32 default OADM, G42 defaults XPDR). G31 and G32 support OADM only; G34c has supported OADM since R7.0. Pre-conditions to configure node-type as OADM: no OMS monitoring-mode in the system may be ila-with-equalization or not-monitored, that is no spectrum (or ochm) objects exist, and no direction-* may exist. Going the other way, to configure node-type as ILA: no OMS monitoring-mode on the dwdm-line ports may be intrusive (no RD or PAx card can exist), no degree, no oxcon and no nmc may exist. Note also that G34c SLTE mode (l0-mode-op slte) is supported only when node-type is ILA, not when it is OADM.

show ne-function. It shows the Network Element generic functions in one listing, which is where the node's directions and amplifiers appear together. The command takes no parameters and is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. A 1830 GX G30 example output lists direction-1 through direction-8, then amplifier-raman-1-7, amplifier-1-1-A, amplifier-1-1-B, amplifier-1-3.1-drop, amplifier-1-5-A, amplifier-1-5-B, amplifier-2-1-A, amplifier-2-1-B, amplifier-2-3-A, amplifier-2-3-B, and finally ne-function itself.

Use set ntp ntp-enabled true and set ntp ntp-auth-enabled true. ntp-enabled takes true/false and defaults to true; ntp-auth-enabled takes true/false and defaults to false, so authentication must be turned on explicitly. The ntp object also carries assignment-method with values manual, dhcp or both (default both), which selects whether the system uses manually configured values, DHCP-supplied values, or both. show ntp displays ntp-enabled, ntp-auth-enabled, ntp-active-server (the currently active NTP server) and assignment-method. The ntp object is managed by the system and cannot be manually added or deleted. Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. To complete authentication, define keys with add ntp-key-<key-id> and point a server at one with set ntp-server-<ip-address> auth-key-id <value>.

NTP keys are created with add ntp-key-<key-id> key-type <value> key-value <value> [is-trusted <value>], and edited/shown/deleted with set, show and delete ntp-key-<key-id>. key-type is the hash algorithm for NTP message digest computation and accepts sha-1, aes-cmac, sha-256 or md5; there is no default, so it must be supplied on add. key-id is a number in the range 1..65534. key-value is a string of length 8..40. is-trusted marks the key as a trusted NTP key and takes true/false, defaulting to false. Example: add ntp-key-2 is-trusted true key-type sha-1 key-value Infinera. Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Yes. The ntp-server object has an origin attribute that is exactly for this: a user can convert a DHCP configured NTP entry into a manually configured one by changing this attribute. Run set ntp-server-<ip-address> origin manual. origin takes dhcp (address assigned to the system by a DHCP server) or manual (address manually configured), and the default is manual. The <ip-address> key may be an IPv4 address, an IPv6 address or a DNS domain name. Other settable attributes on the server are auth-key-id (uint32 or not-applicable, default not-applicable), label, admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock) and alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed). Also check set ntp assignment-method, whose values are manual, dhcp or both, default both, since it governs which configured values the system uses.

Use show ntp-server-status-<ip-address>, for example show ntp-server-status-172.19.13.218. The key field is reach: an 8-bit shift register with the most recent probe in the 2^0 position, where the value 377 indicates that all the recent probes have been answered. Supporting fields are when (seconds elapsed since the last packet was received), poll (polling interval in seconds), delay (path delay to the server in ms), offset (clock offset to the peer in ms), jitter (path jitter in ms), stratum of the remote peer, refid (reference clock type or address), type (local, unicast, multicast or broadcast), auth-status (ok, yes, bad or none, default none) and condition, a string showing values such as sys.peer, reject or candidate. Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

restart [-h] [-f] [<resource-id>] [<type>] [<sub-component>] takes type cold, warm or shutdown, and warm is the default if <type> is not provided. cold reboots all components and sub-components and is service affecting; the system regains connectivity within five minutes. A cold reboot of an XMM4 is not service affecting but visibility is lost; a cold reboot of CHM6, UCM4 and similar is service affecting. warm reboots only the processor of the CHM6, UCM4 and similar and is non service affecting, again regaining connectivity within five minutes; a warm reboot of an XMM4 is non-service affecting but visibility is lost for 3 minutes. shutdown gracefully shuts the card down. If <resource-id> is omitted the active controller card is restarted. Restartable entities are card (cold, warm, shutdown), card sub-component (cold, warm) and tom (cold); not all cards support all types. The command asks for confirmation unless -f is given.

set-time is only applicable when time-source is manual, that is when NTP is not enabled. If the node is synchronising from NTP the manual set is refused; check with show clock time-source (values ntp or manual, default manual) and turn NTP off with set ntp ntp-enabled false before setting the clock by hand. The syntax is set-time [new-time=]<value>, with the value in the ISO 8601 derived combined date and time format 2017-01-12T10:22:25Z, where Z means UTC; a non-UTC timezone is allowed by giving +/-hh:mm instead of Z. Examples: set-time 2021-02-06T11:16:58Z and set-time 2021-04-01T18:46:44+03:00. Access is Operational mode. Read the resulting time back with the time command, which reports it in the system configured timezone rather than the timezone used in the set-time command.

Yes: status equipment. The Equipment dashboard summarises all equipment in the system together with temperature sensors and power values. It lists the chassis, the cards per chassis and their subtype, the toms per card, and per-equipment generic status: presence or absence, oper-state and alarms. The default scope is the entire network element. For large NEs the output can be filtered per chassis by giving the chassis id as the filter, for example status equipment 5; only existing chassis ids are accepted and wildcards are not supported, so you get either all chassis or exactly one.
