Output uses a tick for oper-state enabled, admin-state unlocked or no alarms, a cross for oper-state disabled, and a padlock for admin-state lock; entries show values like temp 25 degrees C and power 2.1/4400 W. Access is Operational mode. Related dashboards are system (the default), L0-oxcon, L0-ocm, L0-spectrum and L1-traffic.

Use clear [-f] system with type factory-reset, for example clear system factory-reset shutdown. The clear system command wipes the system or a specific instance and resets to factory configuration, doing a secure wipe of system data; it stops target traffic services and removes respective files and user configurations, which may imply loss of connectivity. Available types are factory-reset, full-wipe (also reinstalls SW on controller and line cards, requiring a base software reinstall from ONIE to recover) and inactive (clears the inactive software partition). The target may be the entire system or a specific chassis or card AID; if no target is given the entire system is cleared. restart-behavior is either a standard restart (the default) or shutdown, in which case the system does not restart afterwards. -f forces the command without confirmation. Restrictions: factory-reset does not take effect for 1830 GX G30 Optical Carrier-Cards (OCC2T, OCC2E) but is supported for the G30 controller card (FRCU), and clear system factory-reset with the shutdown option is not supported on the L0 cards. For a simple database wipe use clear database instead.

Just type time. The command displays the system's time and takes no parameters; it is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example output: 2020-06-29T22:29:37+00:00. The time reported is based on the system configured timezone. If you want more than the bare timestamp, show clock returns current-time, universal-time (the UTC date and time), timezone, uptime, uptime-seconds, time-source, DST-active and last-time-jump.

The uptime command displays the system uptime and load average, for example: 21:24:09 up 41 days, 15:56, 1 user, load average: 0.10, 0.35, 0.39. The load average, also called average system load, indicates whether there are multiple tasks queued on the system (on the card). Whether it is high or low depends on the number of cores the system has, how many CPUs are integrated into the system or card, and the load average number itself. The rule stated in the guide is that a load average value is considered high when it is greater than the number of CPUs on the card. The command takes no parameters and runs in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. The same uptime figure is also available from show clock uptime and uptime-seconds.

Yes. manual-switchover [-f] [resource=]<value> takes the AID of the object to be switched, and the guide's examples all show the prompt: Controller will switchover and connection to the management interface will be lost. Do you want to continue? [y/n] . You confirm at that prompt to proceed with the manual switch operation, or pass -f to force the command without confirmation. Example resources by chassis: manual-switchover card-1-3 on a 1830 GX G42, manual-switchover card-1-5 on a G32 and manual-switchover card-1-12 on a G34c. Access is Operational mode. For the full procedure, see the 1830 GX Software Management Procedures Guide.

show protection. It displays the node's protection container. The command takes no parameters and is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. From there the more detailed objects are show protection-group-<name>, which reports AID, label, protection-type, pg-state, pg-request, pg-control-request, switching-mode, reversion-mode, hold-off-timer, wtr-timer, remaining-wtr, last-switch-trigger, working-pu, protection-pu, reliable-cp, the four switch triggers, switch-failure-reason and alarm-report-control, and show protection-unit-<protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name>, which reports AID, transport-entity, state, role, alarm-report-control and label.

On protection-group, switching-mode takes unidirectional or bidirectional and defaults to unidirectional. wtr-timer is the trigger clearance soaking time before reverting to the working protection unit, measured and set in 1-second steps, with a range of 60..720 seconds and a default of 300 seconds; it is only applicable in revertive mode. reversion-mode itself takes revertive or non-revertive and defaults to non-revertive, so the WTR timer does nothing until you set revertive. The related read-only remaining-wtr shows the time left in the WTR timer, range 0..720 seconds, again only in revertive mode. The separate hold-off-timer is the switching trigger soaking time before switching, measured and set in 1-millisecond steps, range 0..10000 ms, default 0. All are settable on add protection-group-<name> and set protection-group-<name>.

Use the protection-switch operating command: protection-switch [-f] [operation-type=]<value> [switch-target=]<value> [protection-group=]<value>. For a force onto protection, the guide's example is protection-switch protection-group-test operation-type=force switch-target=protection. operation-type accepts force, lockout, manual or release; switch-target is the target of the switch command and is not needed for the release and lockout operations; protection-group names the group. Access is Operational mode. Equivalently, the protection-group object carries pg-request, whose values are clear (the default), manual-to-working, manual-to-protection, forced-to-working, forced-to-protection, protection-lockout and exercise (exercise applies only to bidirectional SNCP). Clear the switch afterwards with the release operation or pg-request clear.

Query the protection unit: show protection-unit-<protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name> state role. state is the state of the protection-unit and takes active, standby, available or unknown, so the member showing active is the one carrying traffic. role tells you which side of the pair it is, working or protection. The same show also returns AID, transport-entity, alarm-report-control and label. The settable attributes are only alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited, default inhibited) and label, for example set protection-unit-test/1-6-T1 alarm-report-control inhibited. Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. At group level, show protection-group-<name> pg-state and last-switch-trigger explain why the group is where it is.

A small subset of alarms have a raise criteria but no automatic clear criteria and must be acknowledged and cleared manually. Use clear [-f] alarm [alarm-type=]<value> [[resource=]<value>[,<value>]*], for example clear alarm DBRESTOREFAIL; -f forces the command without confirmation. To find which alarms qualify, the alarm-inventory list marks them with can-be-cleared-by-user = true, obtained in CLI with show alarm-inventory can-be-cleared-by-user=true. This mechanism applies only to system alarms that are not associated with any particular resource but with the system itself, that is system wide or global alarms. Access is Operational mode. Separately, set-alarm-state [state=]<value> [[acknowledge-text=]<value>] (all-alarms | [alarm-id-list=]<value>...) changes an alarm's operator state to none, ack or close, taking from 1 up to 10 alarm ids, or all-alarms.

That is governed by the system wide arc-behavior switch on alarm-control: set alarm-control arc-behavior <leave-alarms|clear-alarms>. With leave-alarms, when ARC is set to inhibit the current alarms are left in a raised mode; with clear-alarms, when ARC is set to inhibit the current alarms are cleared. The default is leave-alarms, so by default already-raised alarms stay up. Check the current setting with show alarm-control. The same object also carries alarm-soaking-behavior, with values automatic (soaking time as defined in the FM profile) and no-soak (certain alarms specified in the FM profile have no soaking time), defaulting to automatic; note the OSC LOF alarm uses the per-facility user-configurable lof-soak-timer setting on the PBAx card. Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Per-object inhibition is done with the alarm-report-control attribute (allowed or inhibited) on the object itself.

Look it up in the alarm inventory, which holds all possible alarm types for the system with static information per type: show alarm-inventory-<alarm-type> [resource-type] [alarm-category] [alarm-type-description] [corrective-action] [default-severity] [service-affecting], for example show alarm-inventory-TIM or show alarm-inventory-MSIM. alarm-type-description is the description of the alarm type (string, length 0..128) and corrective-action is system provided information on how to correct the situation that triggered the alarm (string, length 0..256). alarm-category is one of communication, facility, equipment, environmental, processing-error, software, quality-of-service or security. default-severity lists the possible default severities (critical, major, minor, warning, not-reported, event); the same alarm may have different defaults depending on the resource-type. service-affecting is indeterminate, sa, nsa or sa-nsa. Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Yes, that is exactly what alarm-severity-entry is for: it configures the severity for one particular alarm and the entry is keyed by resource type. Use set alarm-severity-entry-<resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location> severity <value>, for example set alarm-severity-entry-OTU2/TIM/ingress/near-end severity minor, or set alarm-severity-entry-tom/EQPTCOMFAIL severity major. resource-type is the card or entity type (CHM1R, FAN, 1830 GX G31 and so on) and alarm-type is the abbreviated code (ADMIN-LOCK, BERSD and so on). direction is na, ingress or egress; location is na, near-end or far-end. severity takes critical, event, major, minor, not-reported or warning. Read it back with show alarm-severity-entry-<...> [severity] [service-affecting], where service-affecting is indeterminate, sa, nsa or sa-nsa; show alarm-severity-entry alone lists all entries. Press ? after the command to list available entities. The object is system managed and cannot be manually deleted.

alarm-severity-profile sets the severity for a whole alarm profile entry rather than for one resource-type/alarm-type/direction/location tuple. Syntax: set alarm-severity-profile <profile-entry> severity <critical|event|major|minor|not-reported|warning>, and show alarm-severity-profile to display; press ? after set alarm-severity-profile to list the available profiles. Example: set alarm-severity-profile alarm-severity-entry-trusted-certificate/CERTIFICATE-EXPIRED severity critical. By contrast alarm-severity-entry is addressed as set alarm-severity-entry-<resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location> severity <value>, so it pins direction (na, ingress, egress) and location (na, near-end, far-end) for a single alarm, and its show also returns service-affecting. Both take the same severity value set, both run in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode, and both objects are managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted.

Use show current-alarms [number-of-alarms] [last-changed]. number-of-alarms is the number of currently raised alarms and last-changed is the timestamp of the last change in the current alarm list, covering either a raise or a clear event. show current-alarms on its own returns the list of currently raised alarms. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For a severity breakdown alongside it, the status system dashboard prints a line such as 13 current alarms (1 critical, 5 major, 2 not-reported, 5 minor). For the alarms themselves use show alarm-<alarm-id> or show alarms, filtering on resource, alarm-type, perceived-severity and similar.

Look at the conditions with get-conditions. A condition is an alarm that is not considered current, which happens when the alarm severity is configured as not-reported or not-alarmed, when the alarm is suppressed due to alarm correlation, when it is suppressed due to ARC (alarm reporting control), or when it is suppressed due to AINS. Syntax: get-conditions [[direction=]<value>] [[resource=]<value>] [[resource-type=]<value>] [[alarm-type=]<value>] [[location=]<value>] [[AID=]<value>]. direction takes all, na, ingress or egress and defaults to all; location takes all, na, near-end or far-end and also defaults to all; resource, resource-type, alarm-type and AID are free filters with no default. Access is Operational mode.

Use set-alarm-state (Operational Mode): set-alarm-state [state=]<value> [[acknowledge-text=]<value>] (all-alarms | [alarm-id-list=]<value>[,<value>]*). state is mandatory; the user can select none, ack or close. Target every raised alarm with the all-alarms option, or name specific alarms with alarm-id-list, which takes from 1 up to 10 alarm ids. acknowledge-text is optional, a string of length 0..256, and it is stored in the alarm itself as user data. Sets to the current state of the selected alarms are accepted, with only the text being updated. Examples: set-alarm-state ack all-alarms acknowledge-text=example, and set-alarm-state ack 28872914984089790,17580406225060810165.

Yes, with clear statistics, which clears the event counters for the specified objects. Syntax: clear [-f] statistics [target=]<value>[,<value>]*, in Operational Mode. target is an instance-identifier and has no default; you can pass a comma separated list. Flags are -h for help and -f to force the command without confirmation. Scope is narrow: currently the only supported object type is aaa-server, and AAA statistics are supported for TACACS+ servers but not for RADIUS servers. Examples: clear statistics aaa-server clears all AAA servers, and clear statistics aaa-server-MyServer clears one named server.

Use show log with the -n and -t options: show [-n=<number>] [-t] log [<logname> [exclude=<exclude-column> ...]]. For example show -n=5 log security shows the last 5 entries. By default log entries are shown in CSV format with each column named in the header; -t gives an alternative table display where columns are aligned, making it easier to read, but potentially making the whole table too wide, in which case drop columns with exclude=<column> after the logname (use tab auto-complete to list removable columns). Valid lognames include security, messages, event, user, alarm, configuration, cli-command, netconf-command, shell-command, kernel, apps, linecard and ztp. You can also pipe, e.g. show log security | exclude john | include NETCONF. Note that due to system restrictions the security log may not be cleared.

Yes, that is the shipped behaviour. The log-console enabled attribute switches console logging on and off, takes true or false, and its default is false, so nothing reaches the console until you turn it on. Enable it with set log-console enabled true, and check it with show log-console [source-facilities] [enabled]. The other attribute is source-facilities, the list of syslog facilities used in this configuration, chosen from all, authentication, clock-daemon-15, clock-daemon-9, ftp-daemon, kernel, line-printer, local1 through local7, log-alert, log-audit, mail-system, network-news, ntp, security, syslog-internal, system-daemons, user-level and uucp. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Add a log-console-facility-filter, a selector that filters messages based on their source facilities and severities: add log-console-facility-filter-<name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>]. The <name> identifies a single syslog facility, or all of them if the value is all. severity takes emergency (0), alert (1), critical (2), error (3), warning (4), notice (5), informational (6) or debug (7), and defaults to informational. compare-op takes equals, equals-or-higher or not-equals and defaults to equals-or-higher. So to suppress informational traffic and keep only serious messages: add log-console-facility-filter-all severity 'critical'. Also available are set, show and delete on the same key. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

It is bounded by two log-file attributes. max-file-size is the maximum file size before rotation in megabytes, a uint8 in the range 1..30, default 30. number-of-files is the maximum number of log files retained, a uint8 in the range 1..20, default 10; when rotating files because max size was reached, the oldest files will be discarded if the total number of files is greater than number of files. So by default a log keeps up to 10 files of up to 30 MB each. Set them with add or set log-file-<name> [number-of-files <value>] [max-file-size <value>]. Locally saved log files can be emptied with clear or removed with delete, but the default system log file cannot be edited or deleted.

Yes. Create the file restricted to that facility and then filter it. First add log-file-<name> source-facilities authentication (source-facilities is a list of syslog facilities, default all); the authentication facility is syslog facility 4, used for authentication/authorization attempts messages. Then optionally narrow severity with add log-file-facility-filter-<log-file-name>/<log-file-facility-filter-name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>], where the filter name is a single syslog facility or all, severity defaults to informational, and compare-op is equals, equals-or-higher or not-equals with default equals-or-higher. Example: add log-file-faults source-facilities all then add log-file-facility-filter-faults/all severity error compare-op equals-or-higher. Related facility security (10) carries security related events and error messages.

Configure with add log-server-<name> address <IP address> ... port <value> transport <udp|tls|tcp>. transport is the transport protocol used when forwarding logs and defaults to udp, so you must state transport tls explicitly. port specifies the port number used to deliver messages to the remote server, range 1..65535, and defaults to 514 unless you say otherwise. message-format identifies the syslog messaging format, either rfc3164 or rfc5424, and defaults to rfc5424. Other defaults: enabled true, message-coalescence true, origin manual, source-facilities all, sensitive-data none, destination-facility-override disabled, alarm-report-control allowed. address takes an IPv4, IPv6 or DNS domain name, and name is a string of length 0...64.

Yes you can filter per collector, but no, it cannot widen anything. Use add log-server-facility-filter-<log-server-name>/<log-server-facility-filter-name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>]. This is a filter based on the source-facilities leaf-list and can only add a filter to the configured source facilities, so it can only narrow what that log-server already forwards. The filter name identifies a single syslog facility, or all of them if the value is all. severity takes emergency, alert, critical, error, warning, notice, informational or debug and defaults to informational; compare-op takes equals, equals-or-higher or not-equals and defaults to equals-or-higher. Example: add log-server-facility-filter-server184/local2 severity debug.

Use the global syslog switch: set syslog remote-logging-switch false. It is a flag to enable remote logging; if false, it disables all remote logging destinations, and its default is true. The configured log-server entries stay in the configuration, so nothing is deleted. Verify with show syslog [remote-logging-switch]. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. A related flag is log-relay, which enables remote logging from a shelf controller to a node controller and defaults to false; if false it disables all remote logging from shelf controller to node controller. Other syslog attributes include source-address (default localhost), assignment-method (both, manual, dhcp; default both), log-file-message-coalescence, niap-compliant-logging and privacy-mode (both default false).

The maximum length of shared-secret is 64 characters. Any value more than 64 characters is denied with an error message. The parameter table lists shared-secret as the shared secret of the aaa server, of type String (length 0...128), with a default value of sharedkey, and it is used in add, set and show; the value is displayed as * rather than in clear text. It is set with add aaa-server-<server-name> ... [shared-secret <value>] or set aaa-server-<server-name> [shared-secret <value>]. For reference, the server-name itself is a string of length 1...64, and common-password is a string of length 1...128.

No, that is expected. For the authentication-requests counter shown by show aaa-statistics-<server-name>, the guide notes that for TACACS+ the default authentication protocol includes both PAP and CHAP, and the authentication requests counter tracks each retry and each authentication protocol attempted independently, so authentication requests may increase by 2 for each retry. The command reports connection-failures (failures due to unavailable servers and timeouts), authentication-requests, authentication-rejects, authorization-requests, authorization-rejects and accounting-requests, all integers. It applies only to AAA servers that use the TACACS+ protocol. Access is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. Counters can be reset with clear statistics aaa-server-<name>.

The ace action attribute is the action taken by the filter, with values drop, accept or reject and a default of drop, so an unspecified match is dropped. Pre-condition: an ACL must be in place before an ACE can be added, and to add an ACE at least one of Source IP / Destination IP / L4 ports / TTL / protocol must be provided. Limits: the sequence-id range is 1-100 for AUX and DCN-B interfaces and 1-256 for the DCN-A interface, and it is recommended to have the sequence-id in multiples of 5 so rules can be inserted later. A maximum of 16 ACEs can be created on an ACL if both upper-port and lower-port values are specified; adding a 17th such ACE returns an error message. Other defaults: direction input, protocol any, ttl 255, logging-action false, ports 0. Example: add ace-TrafficV6/100 action drop source-ip-address 2420::5.

Attach an ACL with add acl-<name> type <value> interface <value> [admin-state <value>]. The interface parameter is a reference to the interface this filter shall be applied to, and the available values are 1-AUX-1, 1-AUX-2, DCN, DCN-B, DCN-2 and DCN-2-B; use add acl-name interface ? to list them. Yes, IPv6 is handled: type indicates the top-level type of ACL, that is what fields from the associated IPv4 or IPv6 headers this ACL matches on, and takes IPv4 or IPv6. name is a string of length 0...30, and admin-state takes lock, maintenance or unlock with default unlock. Note that an ACL can be added on the DCN-B interface when the DCN is operating in active-active configuration. Example: add acl-AuxV4traffic interface 1-AUX-2 type ipv4.

Yes: show access-control-list. That is the whole syntax; the command takes no parameters and is used to show the access control list. Access Mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For the individual objects underneath, use show acl-<name> [admin-state] [oper-state] [avail-state] [type] [interface] for a specific access control list, and show ace-<name>/<sequence-id> for the access control entries within it.

Create an access-rule-list bound to the group, then add a deny rule against the path. For example: add access-rule-list-A user-group XY, then add access-rule-A/<rule-name> path <xpath> operation create,update,delete action deny. Syntax is add access-rule-<access-rule-list-name>/<access-rule-name> action <value> [sequence-id <value>] [module-name <value>] [path <value>] [attribute <value>] [attribute-value <value>] [operation <value>] [description <value>]. action takes permit or deny and is mandatory whenever an access rule is created. path is the target object, an XPath of a YANG data node, notification, RPC or descendant, or an external command, max 255 characters, default *. operation is bits of create, read, update, delete, execute, default * meaning all. Guide example: add access-rule-1/rule path /ne/equipment/card operation create action deny. The system supports a maximum of 500 access-rules across all access-rule-lists.

The access-rule-list is processed in order, as given by the sequence-id parameter, and lower number ids are processed first, so the lowest sequence-id wins first. sequence-id is a uint16; if not provided it is set to the currently used latest id plus 1, so the new entry goes to the end of the list. The id can change over the lifetime of the access-rule-list to re-sort different entries. To say which groups a list applies to, use the user-group attribute: add access-rule-list-<name> [user-group <value>] [sequence-id <value>] [description <value>]. user-group is a leaf-list of user-group names, or '*' which is the default and is a match-all meaning the list applies to all existing user-groups; a maximum of 20 user-groups can be referenced. Example: add access-rule-list-A user-group XY. description is a string of 0..256 characters.

Despite the generic name, auth-key is entirely OSPF scoped: it holds the pre-shared key for OSPFv3 IPsec integrity protection. The key is addressed by a four part AID: add auth-key-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id>/<ospf-if-name>/<spi> key <value> [type <value>], with matching set, show and delete forms. instance-id is the OSPF instance ID, a number in range 0..255; ospf-area-id is the OSPF Router Area ID (string); ospf-if-name references the interface in the OSPF area; and spi is a unique security parameter index for this SA, a number in range 256..4294967295. key is a string of length 8..128, and type indicates whether the integrity key is ASCII or hexadecimal encoded, taking ascii or hex. Example: add auth-key-1/0.0.0.0/DCN/256 key abcdefgh12345678.

Set the global authorization mode to rules-only: set authorization mode rules-only. mode selects which kind of authorization rules are used and takes static-only (only system defined static authorization rules), static+rules (both user and system defined access-rules, with a user configured access-rule looked up first and system rules as fallback) or rules-only (only user defined access-rules; if no rule matches, the global defaults apply). The default mode is static+rules. In rules-only the fallbacks are read-default (default permit; covers get/show and receiving notifications), write-default (default deny; covers create/update/delete) and exec-default (default permit; covers RPC and other command invocation); each takes permit or deny and is only configurable if mode = rules-only. To deny anything the rules do not cover, set all three to deny, e.g. set authorization write-default deny. show authorization also reports denied-operations, denied-data-writes and denied-notifications.

A user changes their own password with the password command in Operational mode: password [old-password=<old-password>] [new-password=<new-password>]. Both the current/old password and the new password must be provided, and this is supported only for local users. A password may contain up to 200 characters. Run password with no arguments for interactive input, where the values are prompted, not echoed, and the new one must be typed twice to confirm; Ctrl+C cancels. Inline form is scriptable but the values are visible: password old-password=Infinera4u! new-password=Infinera4us!. Inline, the special characters \" and ' must be escaped with \, and #?|; must be enclosed in single or double quotes. An administrator does not set another user's password with this command; instead use set user-<username> force-password-change true, which forces that user to change their password on next login.

show security. That is the command used to show the top level security container, and it takes no parameters. Access Mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For the policy flags inside it, use show security-policies, which reports secure-mode, strict-password-check, minimum-password-length, ssh-authentication-method, default-user-group, enforce-password-history-check, password-history-size, aaa-authentication-method, aaa-authorization-method, the ssh and TLS algorithm lists, max-system-sessions, max-local-users and the certificate revocation settings.

Both live under security-policies. minimum-password-length is the configurable minimum length for user passwords, a number in range 1..200 with a default of 8; when a password is changed the length is verified against this policy. strict-password-check defaults to true and enforces minimum length of 8 characters, at least one lower case letter (a-z), one upper case letter (A-Z), one number (0-9) and one symbol, and the user name cannot be part of the password; if disabled, only a minimum length of 1 character is enforced. For history, enforce-password-history-check defaults to true and ensures a new password cannot match any of the previous 5 passwords for the user, and password-history-size is the number of passwords stored for reuse checking, range 1..200, default 5. Both history and strictness policies only affect newly defined passwords once enabled. Set with set security-policies minimum-password-length <value>.

Both thresholds are per-user attributes of the user command. max-invalid-login is the maximum number of consecutive and invalid login attempts before an account is suspended (locked out), a number in range 0-255 with a default of 5. suspension-time is the duration of UID suspension following consecutive invalid login attempts, in minutes, range 0 - 1440, default 5 minutes. Set them with add or set user-<user-name> [max-invalid-login <value>] [suspension-time <value>]. show user-<user-name> reports failed-logins, the number of previous failed logins, which resets to zero upon a successful login, and user-status, which shows lockout when the account is locked out due to unsuccessful login attempts (other values are enabled, disabled and password-aged). Lockout can be turned off globally with the security-policies disable-user-lockout attribute.

show user-data is the whole command. It is used to show the user-data, takes no parameters at all, and its Access Mode is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. For per-user attributes use show user-<user-name>, which returns password-hashed, user-group, display-name, max-invalid-login, suspension-time, timeout, password-aging-interval, password-expiration-date, enabled, user-status, force-password-change, max-sessions, last-login-date, failed-logins, user-aaa-type, alarm-report-control and label.

Use add user-group-<name> [description <value>]; matching set, show and delete forms exist. name is the name of the group, a String of 1...64 characters; description is a long description of the user group, a String of 1...128 characters. Access Mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Each user is associated with a list of groups and derives its permissions from them, assigned via add or set user-<user-name> user-group <value>. Example: add user-group-XY, then delete user-group-XY to remove it. show user-group lists the built-in groups alongside yours: EA Encryption Administrator, MA Monitoring Access, NA Network Administrator, NE Network Engineer, PR Provisioning, SA Security Administrator and TT Turn-up and Test.

Add/Drop Groups are addressed as adg-<adg-number>, where adg-number is an integer in the range [1..110], so a node can have up to 110 ADGs (add adg-1 creates one; delete adg-<n> removes it). Whether the same wavelength can appear twice is reported by the show-only attribute wavelength-duplication, which says whether the SRG can handle duplicate wavelengths and to what extent. Its values are one-per-adg (no duplication of frequencies in the ADG) and one-per-degree (CDC: duplication of frequencies allowed in the ADG, but only one at the Degree). The default is one-per-adg, and only CDCs allow more than one instance of the same wavelength on the ADG. Other show attributes are label (String 0..256), max-add-drop-ports and bands-supported (default standardC-band).

On set amplifier-<name>, control-mode selects auto-max-pw (default, the auto mode targeting maximum output power) or manual. In manual control mode you set gain-target, range 0..40 dB, default 0.0, used to set the gain for constant-gain mode; gain-operating reports the actually configured gain over the same 0..40 dB range. In auto control mode you do not set the gain; instead gain-adjustment applies a user offset in the range [-20.00..20.00], default 0, and it is only supported on amplifiers whose function is pa or inline. Tilt is controlled by tilt-control-mode with values manual, auto (default, system implicitly controls tilt per configured fiber parameters) and auto-planned (system controls tilt per planning tool parameters), so by default the system does control tilt itself. tilt-target ([-5..5] dB, default 0dB) applies only to manual mode and raises the warning that the attribute may be traffic affecting; tilt-adjustment ([-5..5] dB, default 0dB) offsets the target when tilt-control-mode is auto or auto-planned. When the amplifier function is add or drop, the only tilt option is manual.

Use set amplifier-raman-<name> target-raman-gain <value>. The permitted range is [0, 5..30dB] with default 0dB, so you ask for either 0 or a value from 5 to 30 dB. It is configurable only when control-mode is different than auto; when control-mode is auto the parameter is ignored. control-mode values are auto (you configure only the span attributes and optionally the pointloss, gain is controlled automatically), auto-planned (you configure the target Raman gain plus span attributes) and manual (basic manual configuration, even the target pump powers must be configured); the default is auto. To see how many pumps the card has, use show amplifier-raman-<name> number-of-pumps: it reports the number of pumps for the required-equipped card, either 4 or 2, and that value dictates the number of pump-power objects exposed by the system. total-pump-power reports the operating total pump power over [-99..99 dBm], where -99 means no power.

Switch ASE loading on with set ase-idler-service-<name> ase-idler-enable enabled, for example set ase-idler-service-1-8 ase-idler-enable enabled. ase-idler-enable takes enabled or disabled and defaults to disabled; enabled turns on ASE idler signal filling on the unused and nmc-failed portions of the band spectrum. The attribute can also be given on the add ase-idler-service-<name> command, along with alarm-report-control (allowed default, or inhibited). To see whether it actually came up, read the show-only attribute ase-idler-state with show ase-idler-service-<name> ase-idler-state. Its values are ase-enabled (ASE idler signal filling is complete on the band spectrum), ase-partially-enabled (filling is incomplete), ase-faulted (the ASE idler signal is faulted) and ase-disabled (the signal is completely removed from the band spectrum), with default ase-disabled. oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled) and avail-state are also available.

The ASE source output power is set with set ase-idler-source-<name> target-output-power <value>. It is the ASE pump output power required if manually configured, with permitted range (-3.00..20.50) dBm and a default of 13. The pump is not on by default: pump-enable takes enabled or disabled and defaults to disabled, so you must explicitly enable it. The read-only pump-state, which shows the state of the ASE Idler pump, is likewise enabled or disabled with default disabled. A single command can do both, for example set ase-idler-source-1-3.1-ase pump-enable 'enabled' target-output-power '15.00'. Other settable attributes are admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), label (String 0..256) and alarm-report-control (allowed default, or inhibited). The function attribute is fixed at ase-idler-source.

Use the calibrate command, which runs in Operational Mode only, with the syntax calibrate [type=]<value> [trigger=]<value> [entity=]<value>. type has the single value raman, which triggers calibration on raman cards. trigger has the values start, which starts the Raman gain calibration for the OTS span, and stop, which stops it. entity selects the entity to be calibrated and depends on the type parameter; for raman calibration the entity may be an OTS-R entity, given as an instance-identifier. None of the three parameters has a default. To trigger an automatic Raman gain calibration: calibrate raman start ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line. To stop one: calibrate raman stop ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line.

Degrees are addressed as degree-<degree-number>, where degree-number is an integer in the range [1..20] and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees, so a node can have up to 20 degrees (add degree-1 creates one). The spectral granularity is reported by show degree-<degree-number>: slot-width-granularity is the width of a slot with a default of 6250 (value in MHz), and center-freq-granularity, the granularity of allowed center frequencies, defaults to 3125 (value in MHz) with the base frequency for the computation being 193.1 THz per G.694.1. min-slots, the minimum number of slots that may be joined to form a media channel, defaults to 8, and max-slots, the maximum, defaults to 32; min-slots must be less than or equal to max-slots. Also shown are label, is-foadm (default false), wss-less (default true) and bands-supported (default standardC-band).

On a multi-rail ILA node the direction command assigns an index to each DWDM line port, and the system pairs them: direction n and direction n+1 are automatically assigned by the system to the DWDM Line1 and DWDM Line2 ports of the #n C2ILASGH/D2ILASGM card created, where index n is an odd integer with a value between 1 and 15. That is why they come in odd/even pairs: the DWDM Line1 port is always assigned an odd index value and the DWDM Line2 port is always assigned an even index value. The index range is [1..16] (1 and 2 are used when migrating from R6.x). The system sets direction-number from the configured direction-port: 1 when the port is dwdm-line1, 2 when it is dwdm-line2, default 1. direction-port must therefore be port-<shelf>-<slot>-dwdm-line1 for an odd index and port-<shelf>-<slot>-dwdm-line2 for an even index, and the same dwdm-line* port instance can only be selected once per NE. Create with add direction-1 direction-port port-1-3-dwdm-line1; delete -f forces without confirmation.

On a dsc facility the configurable attributes are the ones offered by add dsc-<name> and set dsc-<name>: label (String, length 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock) and alarm-report-control (allowed, meaning alarm reporting is allowed, or inhibited; default allowed). name is the file name without the .log extension, String length 0...128. Everything else is show only: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID (String 1..64), oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled), avail-state and managed-by. The managed-by attribute describes whether this facility was system created or not; its values are system and user with a default of system, and only user-created facilities can be user deleted. So a dsc showing managed-by system cannot be removed with delete dsc-<name>.

On add dsc-group-<name> or set dsc-group-<name> there are four Q signal degrade attributes. Before FEC: pre-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold is the threshold on which the PRE-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE alarm is raised, decimal64 with 3 fraction digits, range 0|5.600..9.600 dB, where 0 implies threshold crossing alarming disabled and the specific sub-range is per carrier use-case; pre-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis is decimal64 with 1 fraction digit, range 0.1..1.0 dB, default 0.5. After FEC: post-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold raises POST-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE, decimal64 with 1 fraction digit, range (12.5..18.0) dB, default 18; post-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis is range (0.1..1.0) dB, default 0.5. Related is dgd-high-threshold, which raises the DGD-OORH alarm, uint16 range (25..400) ps, default 100. Example: add dsc-group-1-3-1-1 rate 100 carriers 1-3-1 group-id 1 instance-id 1.

Use the gadt command, which retrieves information about golden carrier application information. The syntax is show gadt [<application-description-H|application-description-P|application-description-S|application-description-U>], and it is available in both Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. The four parameters application-description-H, application-description-P, application-description-S and application-description-U each give a detailed description of an application ID and are of type string with no default. For example, show gadt application-description-H returns application-description 'Subsea modes using Uniform and Hybrid modulation'. The application IDs H, P, S and U are the same letters used in the application field of a golden carrier mode name such as 800M.95P.

The gapt command lists the golden advanced parameters from the Golden Advanced Parameters Table (GAPT), and it is scoped per card type. The syntax is show gapt-<card-type> [version] [applicable-resource-type], available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. card-type is the card type name (string), version is the table version (string, length 0..5), and applicable-resource-type is the managed resource type(s) applicable for that particular advanced parameter (string); none has a default. Plain show gapt lists the tables per card, for example gapt-CHM6 at version 1.8, gapt-CHM7 at version 3.0 and gapt-CHM7T. Scoping to one card, show gapt-chm7, lists that card's entries such as golden-advanced-parameter-CHM7/BOASetting, golden-advanced-parameter-CHM7/NLC and golden-advanced-parameter-CHM7/RxCDMode, followed by the table's version and applicable-resource-type.

Use the gcmt command, which retrieves information about the golden carrier mode. The syntax is show gcmt [<card-type>] [version], available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode; the object parameter is the golden carrier modes (string) and version is the table version (string), neither with a default. To look up a specific mode, name it directly: show gcmt golden-carrier-mode-800M.95P. The output lists the mode with its capacity (Gbps), client-mode, baud-rate (GBaud), application, compatibility-id and status, for example golden-carrier-mode-CHM6/800M.95P with capacity 800, client-mode ethernet-otn, baud-rate 95.2965203, application P, compatibility-id 6 and status supported. For the full per-attribute view use show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode>.

Read the status attribute with show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode> status, which describes the carrier mode release status. Its values are supported, candidate, experimental, deprecated and diagnostic, with no default, so a mode showing supported is fully supported while one showing experimental is not. The same status column appears in show gcmt output alongside capacity, client-mode, baud-rate, application and compatibility-id, for example golden-carrier-mode-CHM6/800M.95P with status supported. Two related attributes qualify this per subtype: supported-subtypes lists the subtypes that each carrier mode supports (string length 0...32, maximum 20 elements), and candidate-subtypes lists the subtypes for which this carrier mode has candidate status (string length 0..16, maximum 10 elements). Both the gcmt and golden-carrier-mode commands run in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use the l0-capabilities command, which shows the capabilities details related with the node's Layer 0 functions. The syntax is simply show l0-capabilities. It takes no command parameters at all, and it is available in both Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. For the photonic node's structural limits specifically, the companion command is show oadm-capabilities [max-degrees] [max-adgs], which reports the maximum number of degrees (20) and the maximum number of ADGs (110).

A Media Channel is carved out with add mc-<name>, and three arguments are mandatory: parent-oms, lower-frequency and upper-frequency. parent-oms is an instance-identifier set only upon MC creation, and its referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree, it cannot be in an ADG. lower-frequency and upper-frequency are the lower and upper frequencies of the media channel, given as values in MHz. Optional arguments on add are label (String 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed default, or inhibited) and auto-delete (disabled default, or enabled; enabled is only allowed on RD66TM sleds with l0-mode-op=hsc-ols and is always disabled if l0-mode-op is standard or slte). The system derives center-frequency and slot-width, the latter calculated as upper-frequency minus lower-frequency. Example: add mc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 parent-oms '1-3.1-dwdm-line' lower-frequency '192225000' upper-frequency '192300000'.

The Media Channel Filler is read only. The mc-f command is used only to show the Media Channel Filler facility attributes, and its sole syntax is show mc-f-<name> [supporting-facilities] [supported-facilities] [supporting-card] [supporting-port] [AID] [lower-frequency] [upper-frequency] [slot-width]. There is no add, set or delete form, and every parameter in the table is marked as used in show only. The attributes are name (String 0..64), supporting-facilities and supported-facilities (instance identifiers to parent and children facilities), supporting-card and supporting-port (leafrefs), AID (String 1..64), lower-frequency and upper-frequency of the MC Filler in MHz units, and slot-width, calculated by the system from upper-frequency minus lower-frequency. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. By contrast, the Network Media Channel Filler command nmc-f does allow set of admin-state and alarm-report-control.

Cards are attached to an Add/Drop Group with add modules-adg-<adg-number>/<index> supported-card <value> [ocm-monitoring <value>]. adg-number is a number in the range [1..110] and index is a number in the range [1..4], so up to 4 cards can be put into one ADG. The card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). supported-card is the instance of the card for the ADG. Channel monitoring is on by default: ocm-monitoring takes true or false with a default of true. It is set upon creation and cannot be changed after supported-card has been assigned, but it can optionally be configured to false for OMD cards directly connected to PAx/BAX or C2ILASGH degrees, for example FOADM nodes. The command runs in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode for Network Administrator and Network Engineer. Example: add modules-adg-1/1 supported-card card-1-6.

Use add modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> supported-card <value>. degree-number is a number in the range [1..20] and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees. index has the single permitted value 1, and the card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). supported-card is an instance identifier for the card or subcard that belongs to the degree; in R6.0 the card must be RD09SM or RD20TM. You can afterwards change it with set modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> supported-card <value>, read it back with show modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> [supported-card], and remove the association with delete modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index>. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode, for Network Administrator and Network Engineer. Example: add modules-degree-1/1 supported-card card-1-1.

Use show monitored-channel-<name>/<frequency> monitored-optical-power. The name corresponds to the (WS04S) card name with the suffix -1 or -2, for ocm1-in or ocm2-in respectively, and frequency is the nominal center frequency of the carrier (channel) in MHz, a uint32. monitored-optical-power is the measured power for the corresponding carrier (channel) in dBm, decimal64 with range (-99.00..99.00) and default -99, where the value -99.00 means no power. The other show attribute is monitored-width, the carrier (channel) width configured at the NMC within the oxcon source/destination, in MHz, uint32, default 0. The command is show only, in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. Example: show monitored-channel-1-1.2-ocm1-in/195987500 monitored-optical-power, or omit the attribute to see all of them.

On add nmc-<name>, center-frequency is mandatory and is the nominal center frequency of the NMC, with permitted values in the range [190650000..196700000] MHz. width is the network media channel frequency width in MHz, with values in the range [15000..200000] MHz and a default of 35000. The user must configure the 3 dB signal bandwidth, and the value in GHz must be equivalent to the baud rate in GBd configured on the connected transponder line interface line port. Both center-frequency and width are used in add and show only, so they are fixed at creation. The other mandatory creation argument is parent-facility, which can be either a Media Channel or an OMS, is only set upon creation, and whose referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree and cannot be in an ADG. Example: add nmc-cdc-1-4_192800000-34000 center-frequency 192800000 width 34000 parent-facility oms-1-4-ad1.

The Network Media Channel Filler occupies a default alloc-bandwidth of 75000, a value in MHz units, which is the allocated bandwidth of the NMC Filler. It is paired with alloc-lower-frequency and alloc-upper-frequency, the allocated lower and upper frequencies in MHz, neither of which has a default. The actually occupied spectrum is reported separately by actual-lower-frequency, actual-upper-frequency and actual-bandwidth, and actual-bandwidth defaults to 0. It is monitored: monitoring-state indicates whether the NMC is intended to be in use, and because this is a system created attribute it is enabled by default, with values enabled and disabled. All these are show only; on nmc-f only admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock) and alarm-report-control (allowed default, or inhibited) can be set. Power is read via power-actual-tx and power-actual-rx, each [-99.00..99.00] dBm with default -99. Example: show nmc-f-1-3-dwdm-line-58.

Use show oadm-capabilities [max-degrees] [max-adgs], available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. max-degrees is the maximum number of degrees and reports 20 (uint8); it is 0 if not supported, degrees are only supported in OADM node types, and by convention the maximum degrees for the ILA node-type is 0 because an ILA has only 2 directions, fixedly, which is not shown in supported capabilities. The maximum number of degrees is not necessarily the deployment supported configuration, but the maximum number of a working degree-number. max-adgs is the maximum number of Add/Drop Groups and reports 110 (uint8); it is 0 if not supported, and ADGs are only supported in OADM node types. Typical output is max-degrees 20 and max-adgs 110. These match the degree-number range [1..20] and adg-number range [1..110].

On set oc-<name> the loopback attribute takes facility, terminal or none, with a default of none, and is useful to debug on the fiber connection; loopback-mode indicates the loopback action for facility or terminal and takes facility or terminal with no default. For test patterns, test-signal-type is the type of test pattern that is injected, with values none, enumeration, PRBS31Q, PRBS13Q, scrambled-idles, PRBS9 and PRBS31, defaulting to none. test-signal-direction is the direction of the test signal and has the single value ingress, default ingress. test-signal-monitoring monitors the incoming test signals for diagnostics and takes true or false, default false. All five attributes are readable through show oc-<name>. The command runs in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: set oc-1-5-T9.1 test-signal-monitoring false.

On an ILA node the OCHm represents the signaled optical channel from OSC, detected at the ILA OMS by using the OSC information; that is, the optical channel monitoring information is derived from the Optical Supervisory Channel rather than measured per channel locally. Consequently, when either the OMS monitoring-mode is not-monitored (as configured by the user), or there is no OSC messaging information, the list of OCHm facilities in the NE will be empty. Read the facilities with show ochm or show ochm-<name>, for example show ochm-1-7-dwdm-line2-191968750-egress avail-state. direction is ingress or egress but currently only egress is supported, default egress. power-actual is the currently received power in dBm, where -99dBm means the power is not yet measured (measurement is performed by the OCM at DGE2 card) or no power was detected; for egress it should be calibrated at the DWDM Line port output. Settable attributes are label, admin-state and alarm-report-control.

Use `show ocm-channel-<name>/<lower-frequency>/<upper-frequency>`. The ocm-channel object lists the detected carriers within the configured OXcon(s), and is show-only (Operational Mode, Candidate Configuration Mode). Fields: name (String length 0..64), lower-frequency and upper-frequency (uint32) which are the lower/upper frequency of the corresponding spectrum power (OPM-pwr point), opm-pwr (Optical Parameter Monitor power in dBm, decimal64 range -99.00..99.00, default -99), and connected (true/false, default false), which yields 'true' if the channel is configured, that is, involved in an oxcon. Example: `show ocm-channel-<name>/<lower-frequency>/<upper-frequency> opm-pwr connected`.

Yes. On ocm-mp the attribute ocm-enable, which enables regular power monitoring, takes disabled or enabled and defaults to enabled. Change it with `set ocm-mp-<name> ocm-enable disabled`. The full set command is `set ocm-mp-<name> [label] [admin-state] [ocm-enable]`; admin-state takes lock, unlock or maintenance with default unlock. Read-only companions: monitoring-state, which the system reports as enabled when an OMS reference exists (default enabled); monitored-port, the port being monitored, default not-applicable, which can differ from supporting-port for a non-integrated OCM; and ad-direction, the reference to the AD (coupler/splitter) DWDM port, which for ocm-mp is only ingress. ocm-mp is managed-by system.

The ocm-ptp facility is available for WS04S cards within a CD-AD ADG and provides dedicated OCM monitoring. It is not enabled out of the box: ocm-enable (enabled/disabled) defaults to disabled, so turn it on with `set ocm-ptp-1-1.2-ocm1-in ocm-enable enabled`. The set command also takes label and admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock). Show-only attributes include ad-direction (egress or ingress, default ingress), last-measurement (last OCM scan date-and-time, or never, default never), adg-number (uint8 range 0..110, default 0) and monitoring-state (default disabled; the system reports enabled when complete connectivity at the AD is established and OCM measurement is possible).

On the oms facility, grid-mode defaults to flexible, which lets you create and delete MCs of different widths. The alternatives are fixed-50G-96ch, fixed-100G-48ch, fixed-75G-64ch, fixed-75G-64ch-oif (R6.0.1 and later), fixed-50G-7100 (50GHz, 88 channels, set automatically when osc-compatibility is osc-7100, R7.0 and later) and fixed-150G-40ch. Default lower-frequency is 191300000 and upper-frequency 196150000 (standardC-band). monitoring-mode selects the monitoring/equalization behaviour: not-monitored (non-intrusive monitoring, no OCM/DGE required), intrusive (TTP), non-intrusive (CTP, operates with OCM such as DGE), dge-fixed-attenuation (fixed attenuation due to a connected interstage device), ila-with-equalization (operate with DGE and OCM) and integrated-equalization (integrated DGE). Default is intrusive for all node types except ILA, not-monitored for node-type ILA and integrated-equalization for hyperscale ILA nodes. It is only exposed for an OMS of a port that belongs to a degree, or on an ILA node.

`set ops-<name>` accepts label, admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed), input-psd-profile, role and port-expansion. input-psd-profile is the nominal expected tributary channel power density in dBm/12.5GHz, decimal64 range -30..-6, default -6. role can be tributary (single add/drop to a local or remote transponder), multi-carrier (multiple carriers on the underlying filter port), general-purpose (the default, used for express cross-connection to another filter), ase-input (only available on specific RD ports in SLTE l0-mode-op) or active-multi-carrier (multiple carriers with active port control). supported-roles is read-only and exposes which roles the card, and sometimes the card-mode, permits. port-expansion is no (default) or y-cable. Example: `set ops-1-6-ad1 role tributary`.

On optical-carrier, frequency is the center frequency the carrier is tuned to, 0 meaning not configured; the generic range is 0 | 191275000..196125000 MHz but the real range and step depend on module and pluggable, for example CHM7 and CHM7X 190625000-196725000 MHz (step 50 MHz), CHM6 191333000-196117000 MHz (step 50 MHz), CHM2TX 191292500-196137500 MHz (step 1 MHz), TOM-400G-C-DWDM 191275000-196125000 MHz. tx-power is the transmit power into the fiber, overall range -55.0..55.00 dBm, adjustable in steps of 0.5 dBm, with per-module limits such as CHM2TX -6 to 0 (default 0), CHM7/CHM7X -10 to 0 (default -2) and UTM2 -15 to 0 (default -6.0); on TOM-100GFI-C-DWDM and the 10GMR SFP+ pluggables it is not configurable. For a slight trim use frequency-offset, int16 range -6000..6000 MHz, default 0: once set the frequency changes slowly over 1-10 s without affecting service.

Yes. `set optical-carrier-<name> propagate-shutdown enabled`. When propagate-shutdown is set, the transmit laser is shut down if the whole service of that direction has signal failure; the function is mainly used at a regeneration node to propagate signal failure as LOS. Values are enabled and disabled, default disabled. Pair it with propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer, the hold off time of propagate shutdown, range 0..2000 milliseconds, default 0. Restriction: neither propagate-shutdown nor propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer is configurable on the SPN2 or SPN2C card.

Very little. `set optical-channel-<name>` accepts only label (String length 0..256) and admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), for example `set optical-channel-channel1 admin-state unlock`. Everything else is read-only through `show optical-channel-<name>`: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID (String length 1..64), oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled), avail-state, and managed-by (system or user, default system; only user-created facilities can be user deleted). Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Read laser-state on the optical-ptp: `show optical-ptp-<name> laser-state`. It shows the emitting pump (for example booster) laser state as enabled or disabled, default disabled, and is only of relevance for DWDM line ports; on RD amplifiers it refers to the source (Tx) pump, on Raman modules to the pump laser. Yes, you can declare fixed pad on the receive side: fix-rx-attenuation is the fixed attenuator before port Rx, decimal64 with 2 fraction digits, range 0..30 dB, default 0, where 0 dB is equivalent to no fixed attenuator. Example: `set -f optical-ptp-1-6-dwdm fix-rx-attenuation 10`. There is a matching fix-tx-attenuation (fixed attenuator after port Tx, 0..30 dB, default 0) but it is only visible when ops.port-expansion=y-cable is configured. Measured levels are power-actual-rx and power-actual-tx (-99.00..99.00 dBm, default -99 dBm).

On optical-switch the Signal Fail thresholds are working-los-threshold and protection-los-threshold, both settable, both optical power in the range -55.0 to 0 dBm with default -23 dBm; received power below that declares the path failed. There is also facility-los-threshold, the threshold of the facility port below which loss of signal is declared, range -55 to 15 dBm, default -30.0 dBm. Signal Degrade switching uses working-switch-threshold and protection-switch-threshold (-55.0 to 0 dBm, default -18 dBm) and is only active when switch-threshold-enable is enabled (default disabled). Hysteresis is configurable: los-threshold-hysteresis (SF, default 3 dB) and switch-threshold-hysteresis (SD, default 2 dB), both decimal64 range 0.5 to 5.0 dB in steps of 0.1 dB, with 1 dB recommended for MCHP and OMSP deployments.

`set osc-<name>` accepts label, admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed), l0-comm-interface-type (ipv4 or ipv6; ipv4 for standard OLS, ipv6 for SLTE and HSC OLS), osc-control (auto or manual, default auto; auto is supported from R6.0.1 and HSC OLS nodes support auto only), target-output-power (na, or -2.5..4.5 dBm, default na, defined at the DWDM Line port output), tx-power-adjustment (na for IR and LR OSC SFP types, or -6..6 dB, default 0, adjusting the automatically calculated Tx target in osc-control auto mode), voa-attenuation-target-rx (0..30 dB, default 10, used in manual control mode) and lof-soak-timer (short, effectively about 3 ms, default; or long, adding 18,400 OC-3 frames, about 2300 ms; only visible for the PBAx card and affecting OSC LOF alarm timing only). Read-only: monitoring-mode, oscc-support, osc-mode, osc-wavelength, voa-attenuation-actual-rx, power-actual-rx and power-actual-tx.

Use `show otdr-<name> otdr-state`. otdr-state indicates the current status of the OTDR and a status change triggers a change notification: not-available (default), idle, measuring (measurement ongoing), finished (measurement completed) or fail (measurement failed). Alongside it, otdr-measurement-time gives the time remaining in the running measurement (default 0), otdr-error carries the error message produced when the measurement ends with error, otdr-laser-state shows not-available/enabled/disabled, otdr-measurement-port shows the port being measured (0 means the card is not measuring any port), otdr-measurement-direction shows not-available/tx/rx (not-available means the scan is not running) and otdr-ongoing-measurement-profile shows none, short, medium, long or raman-precheck1/2/3. Per-port results such as otdr-last-measurement, otdr-last-measurement-file and otdr-fiber-break-distance are on otdr-ptp.

On otdr-ptp: otdr-range specifies the distance range in kilometers used to calculate the measurement repetition period, auto (default) or 0...300.0 km, and it is recommended to set the actual fiber length plus 10%; from R9.1, when the OTS can be traced from the fiber connection between the ILA/ROADM card and OTDR8OFP2, auto is derived from OTS fiber-length-tx/fiber-length-rx with 10% margin rounded up to the nearest 10 km. otdr-resolution is the data sampling resolution, auto or 0.4...100.0. otdr-pulse-width is auto or 10...20,000 ns and determines dynamic range together with the other parameters. otdr-measurement-speed is fast (about 10 s), medium (about 15 s), slow (about 1 minute), precision (about 3 to 5 minutes), high-precision (about 5 to 7 minutes) or auto (default). Also otdr-ior (auto, or 1.0...2.0), peak-power (auto, or 5...14.5) and launching-fiber-length (0...50 m, default 0; auto is not supported), which is deducted from the result.

On the ots facility. `set ots-<name>` takes fiber-type-tx and fiber-type-rx, chosen from AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, SSMF, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS and VistaCor, both defaulting to SSMF (fiber-type-rx also accepts not-applicable, auto and not-configured). Lengths are fiber-length-tx and fiber-length-rx, auto by default or 0..500.0 km, required for tilt control when tilt-control-mode = auto and when Raman backward pumping is deployed. Loss is declared with span-loss-transmit and span-loss-receive, decimal64 range 0..80 dB (receive also 99), default 0; changing span-loss-receive is traffic affecting. Non-fiber loss such as patch panels goes in external-attenuation-tx and external-attenuation-rx (0..30 dB, default 0). Also span-loss-aging-margin-rx (0.00..10.00 dB, default 1.0), fiber-spectral-attenuation-tilt-tx/rx (-1..1 dB/THz) and raman-coefficient-tx/rx (0..10 dB/THz/W). span-loss-reference (configured or measured, default measured) selects which value power control uses; derived values appear in fiber-length-derived-rx/tx and span-loss-derived-rx/tx.

The system generates it. The ots-diagnostics name is auto generated on line card provisioning, with the format 'ots-diagnostics-<chassis>-<slot>-<DWDM Line>', so you address it as, for example, `show ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line` for an RD20TM DWDM line, or ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line1 and ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line2 for a C2ILASGH with two lines. Only two attributes are settable: nmoper-alarm-reporting (disabled by default; when enabled, a mismatch between expected-operator and rx-operator raises the NMOPER alarm, and disabling it clears the alarm immediately and stops the comparison) and expected-operator (up to 32 characters/bytes, empty by default). tx-operator is automatically defaulted by the system with the format '<ne-name>-<Dxx>', default <ne-name>-D00.

ots-r assumes SSMF. required-fiber-type-rx is the required fiber type on the DWDM Line with reference to the Rx fiber, default SSMF, selected from AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, SSMF, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS and VistaCor; it is only of relevance if control-mode = auto and when there is no fiber-connection. The rest of the receive span is declared with fiber-length-rx (unspecified by default, or 0..500.0), span-loss-receive (default 99), external-attenuation-rx, delta-pointloss (not-applicable by default, or -1..3.5 dB, the fiber contribution to point loss to be fine tuned in the field, for example a bad splice at dwdm-line Rx) and target-power-setting (manual or auto, default auto), plus label, admin-state (default unlock) and alarm-report-control (default allowed). Read-only: configured-fiber-type-rx, configured-fiber-length-rx, span-loss-at-amplifier, power-actual-rx and connected-reference.

Yes, and yes. `set ots-r-auto-otdr-<name> automatic-otdr enabled|disabled` enables or disables the OTDR based automatic fiber check. The default is enabled for green field deployments and disabled for in-field SW upgrade. In addition, if the Raman card is associated with a base card equipped with an integrated OTDR the default is enabled, and if the NE has a Raman card that is not aggregated with the EDFA card the value is disabled. The setting persists over warm and cold restart and over SW upgrade. Disabling it while a test is running aborts the ongoing OTDR test and allows the amplifier blocked by the automatic OTDR to be activated; when enabled, tests are triggered at the next opportunity when the pre-conditions and triggering criteria are met. Progress is shown by auto-otdr-state (not-applicable, not-available, pass, in-progress, fail, aborted) and results by external-attenuation-rx-measured (0..55 dB) and total-reflectance-rx-measured (-99..99 dB). loss-calibration-by-otdr (none default, rx-only, tx-only, tx-rx) decides whether measured values feed Power Control.

Use `add oxcon-<name> source <value> destination <value>` with the two media channel end-points, for example `add oxcon-1-80-192262500__1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 source 'nmc-1-80-192262500' destination 'nmc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500'`. Optional on add: label, activation-mode, auto-delete, activation-request-fwd/bwd, direction (two-way default, or one-way), target-output-power-src and target-output-power-dst (decimal64 range -18.00..15.00 dBm; default 0 dBm, or -5 dBm when an Add/Drop OXcon is created between a Tributary NMC and an RD20TM/RD09SM NMC) and circuit-id. Whether it comes up on its own depends on activation-mode: automatic, the default in standard L0 mode, activates the service automatically on creation and deactivates it on deletion; manual (SLTE mode) and activate-on-create (HSC OLS mode) are driven manually through activation-request-fwd and activation-request-bwd (no-request, activate, deactivate), with activation-state-fwd/bwd reporting activated, partially-activated, faulted or deactivated.

profile-control applies only to RD20TM operating in card-mode = slte or slte-backhaul, and only in Operational Mode. Syntax: `profile-control [type=]<value> [entity=]<value> [direction=]<value> [[profile-data=]<value>]`. type is write-attenuation-profile, read-attenuation-profile, create-power-profile, read-power-profile or read-ocm-power; entity references the object (an OMS or an NMC); direction is tx or rx, and for power-profile only tx is supported. Example: `profile-control read-power-profile oms-1-8-dwdm-line tx`. For RD20TM in card-mode = slte the power profile and OCM power are defined at the output of the booster, before the EVOA, not at the DWDM line out port. The OMS attenuation string is '<StartFreq>,<SlotWidth>,<AttnValue1>,...,<AttnValueN>' with StartFreq in MHz, SlotWidth in GHz, attenuation values 0 to 25.50 and N = 776 for standardC-band at 6.25 GHz granularity; for NMC the values range -10 to 25.50 and N cannot exceed 32.

Not much. `set pump-<name>` accepts only label (String length 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance) and alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited, default Allowed). Everything else on the pump command is show-only: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled/disabled), avail-state (in-service, out-of-service, normal, abnormal, low-power), managed-by (system or user, where only user created facilities can be user deleted) and pump-type. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Pump power levels are not on this command: use pump-power for target-pump-power, configured-pump-power and actual-pump-power.

Use `set pump-power-<name>/<pump-id> target-pump-power <value>`, where pump-id is an integer identifying the number of the pump. target-pump-power is the Raman pump power required, in dBm, and applies when the control-mode is manual; permitted values are -99.00..99.00 dBm or not-applicable (the default), with 0 used for the not-applicable case. If the card is RPBM, target-pump-power must be in the range 12 to 30 dBm. If the value is outside the operating range of the Raman sled, the alarm PUMP-Fail (STAT FAIL PSTAT) is raised. How high it may go is reported by max-target-pump-power, with min-target-pump-power for the lower bound; both are decimal64 with 2 fraction digits, range -99.00..99.00 dBm, or not-applicable. configured-pump-power shows the value programmed in hardware (derived automatically when control-mode is auto, otherwise from target-pump-power) and actual-pump-power the currently measured value (default -99).

Use `show raman-calibration-<name> calibration-state`, for example `show raman-calibration-1-8`. calibration-state displays the state of the automatic Raman gain calibration process: not-available (the default: calibration has not been triggered or no prior calibration has occurred), in-progress (currently running), up-to-date (completed successfully and current), out-dated (stale due to OTS OLOS, a change in delta pointloss and similar) or fail (ended with a failure). Supporting read-only fields: last-calibration-timestamp (date-and-time, or never, default never), gain-calibration-error (residual gain error after each iteration in dB, or not-available), calibrated-delta-pointloss (suggested delta-pointloss at the end of each iteration, -3..3.5 dB, or not-available), intermediate-results (string up to 1024), and additional-info, which carries troubleshooting information when calibration-state is fail or out-dated. The only settable attribute is label.

rsc is the Raman card Pilot Tone facility. `set rsc-<name>` takes label, admin-state (Unlock, Locked, Maintenance, Unknown; default Unlocked) and alarm-report-control (Allowed or Inhibited, default Allowed). It reports two Pilot Tone measurements: rsc-power-rx, the received Pilot Tone integrated power, and rsc-power-tx, the transmitted Pilot Tone integrated power. The remaining show fields are supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled or disabled, default enabled), avail-state and managed-by (system or user, default system; only user created facilities can be user deleted). Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Because the OMS underneath is not in a monitoring-mode that creates it. The spectrum facility is only instantiated by the system when the underlying server layer, OMS, has monitoring-mode configured either as non-intrusive or ila-with-equalization; the existence of this managed object depends on the OMS monitoring-mode. The object is only of relevance if the DGE2 is intended to be used in the NE. Set the OMS monitoring-mode accordingly and the spectrum object appears. On the object, dge-in-use reports true if the corresponding OMS monitoring-mode is ila-with-equalization (default false), and attenuation-setting is the unique attenuation value for the entire spectrum, range 0..30 dB, default 0 dB, editable when attenuation-control-mode = manual and control-mode = auto-max-pw.

Use spectrum-control, which is keyed by name, direction and center-frequency: `set spectrum-control-<name>/<direction>/<center-frequency> attenuation-target <value>` or target-output-power, for example `set spectrum-control-1-7-dwdm-line2/egress/194943750 attenuation-target 1`. direction is ingress or egress, but only egress is currently supported (default egress). center-frequency is the band slice center frequency in MHz and is managed by the system. attenuation-target is the required attenuation for the spectra, range 0..30 dB, default 0, and is only possible to configure when a Dynamic Gain Equalizer, or equivalent, is in use (dge-in-use = 'true'). target-output-power is the intended target output power, not-specified (default) or -55..55 dBm. Read-only: attenuation-actual, only readable when a DGE is in use, and width, the detected width from spectrum-monitoring in MHz, which returns 0 if the configured center-frequency matches no spectrum or if no ILAx card or DGE is fiber-connected.

Use `show spectrum-monitoring-<name>/<direction>/<center-frequency> [width] [lower-frequency] [upper-frequency] [target-actual-power] [power-actual] [psd-actual]`, available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. name is a string 0..64; direction is ingress or egress, default egress, and only egress is currently supported; center-frequency is the band slice centre in MHz, managed by the system. width is the received NMC width in MHz, default 50000. lower-frequency and upper-frequency give the media channel edges in MHz. power-actual is the currently received power in dBm, default -99; -99 dBm means the power has not yet been measured by the OCM on the DGE2 card, or no power was detected (or no appropriate fiber-connection). In the egress direction the power actual is calibrated at the DWDM Line port output, the same reference point where target power is defined. target-actual-power is the power calculated by ATPS and is only relevant when target-power-setting = auto; with manual it shows the default -99dBm. psd-actual is the calculated Power Spectral Density in nW/GHz to 2-digit precision, default not-applicable, and does not depend on the spectra width. Example: `show spectrum-monitoring-1-7-dwdm-line2/egress/191968750`.

Read the `contention-check-status` attribute on the super-channel. It is settable on `add super-channel-<name> carriers <value> carrier-mode <value> [label] [admin-state] [alarm-report-control] [contention-check-status <value>]` and readable with `show super-channel-<name> ... [contention-check-status]`. The values are pending, success, overridden and failk, with pending as the default. It is the Contention Check state set via DNA in openwave mode, and it is only applicable if `openwave-contention-check` is enabled at the super-channel-group level. That attribute enables the DNA assisted contention control mechanism in openwave mode; its values are false and true, default false. Related state on the same object: admin-state (lock, maintenance, unlock; default unlock), line-system-mode default openwave, and expected-total-tx-power, the theoretical total TX power at the faceplate computed from the per-carrier target TX power, default -55.

The `-m` flag means merge configuration: the command will not fail if the entity already exists. The add command for super-channel-group works in merge mode only, so `-m` performs a best effort add. If the target entity does not exist it is created; if it already exists it is updated with any attributes present on the add command. Full syntax: `add -m super-channel-group-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <lock|unlock|maintenance>] [auto-in-service-enabled <value>] [valid-signal-time <value>] [alarm-report-control <allowed|inhibited>] [line-system-mode <value>] [openwave-contention-check <value>]`, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. Defaults on those attributes: admin-state unlock, alarm-report-control allowed, auto-in-service-enabled false, valid-signal-time 480 minutes (range 1..7200), line-system-mode openwave, managed-by user. The same merge flag and note apply to `add -m comm-channel-<name>`.

Use `show supported-carrier-mode-<name>/<carrier-mode> [capacity] [client-mode] [baud-rate] [application] [compatibility-id] [status] [supported-subtypes]`, in Operational or Candidate configuration mode. carrier-mode is an acronymized code (handle) indicating the optical carrier line mode 4-tuple, string length 1...15, formatted <Capacity><ClientMode>.<Baud Rate><Application ID>, for example 600E.84P, 100X.73U or 325M.66P. capacity is the net capacity of the optical carrier, in gbps. client-mode gives the digital client modes of the signal mapped into and transported by the carriers within the superchannel: ethernet or ethernet-otn. baud-rate is the modulated symbol rate. application is the optical transport application ID the mode is optimized for, string length 1...15. compatibility-id identifies the carrier modes that can be applied simultaneously. status is the state of the carrier mode. supported-subtypes lists the subtypes each carrier mode supports, string 0..32, maximum 20 elements.

Use `show supported-gain-range-<name>/<gain-range-type> [gain-range-min] [gain-range-max]`, available in Operational and Candidate configuration mode. gain-range-type takes low, high or standard. gain-range-min is the minimum settable gain-target for that type of range ('standard'/'low'/'high') and gain-range-max is the maximum settable gain-target for that range; both are of type gain-value, with no default (n/a). So issuing the show against a given gain-range-type returns the concrete min and max gain-target figures the amplifier will accept for that range. The name key in the parameter table is documented as a flag to enable or disable access control, values true or false, default false.

Different power profiles can be supported to reflect different scenarios when using a card.
